L00_N0267_neg.wrong_label: Tokens right after a number that make it a measured quantity: units of time, money, length, weight, volume or count ('minutes', 'hours', 'weeks', 'month', 'years', 'gallons', 'ounces', 'carat', 'm2', 'in.'). Rate and distribution words that follow those units fire as well, often more strongly: 'per', 'each', 'a month', 'apart', 'side', 'person', 'session', 'discount'. Example: '$20 a month' gives month +6, and '5 minutes on each side' gives each +6. The digits themselves are weakly positive (+1 to +3), mostly the last digit. Spelled-out numbers count too: 'another five minutes' gives five +5.

L00_N0338_neg.wrong_label: The word 'minimum'/'Minimum' used as a lower-bound threshold (minimum wage, minimum order, minimum of, minimum investment, minimum requirements). The word itself peaks at about +8 to +10. The following token is often also elevated (+3 to +9): 'of', 'order', 'purchase', 'investment', 'for', 'is'. Weaker cousins of the lower-bound idea also fire: 'minimal'/'minimally' (+4 to +5), 'at least' (on 'least', +2 to +3), 'no fewer than' (+3), 'as little as' (+3), 'as soon as possible' (+3), 'shortest distance between' (+4 to +8), and 'min' as in 'minification' (+3).

L00_N0833_pos.wrong_label: American or industrial crop-agriculture and food-production discourse: GMOs and non-GMO labels, genetically engineered commodity crops (corn, soy, alfalfa), organic fertilizers, agribusiness, no-till/tillage, greenhouse production systems, cover crops on corn and soy, USDA zones, cornstarch, nutrient-deficient fields, farming techniques in development projects. Negative values are spread over function words and punctuation inside these lists, e.g. '(', ',', 'are', 'of', 'on', 'in'. It also fires on lowercase 'd' fragments starting words (d|rench, d|rier, anti-d|iscrimination) and weakly on 'D' in Indian or US abbreviations (DTC).

L00_N1399_neg.wrong_label: Tokens naming human or natural processes, activities or impacts acting on such environments: trawling/trawlers, algae blooms, salinization, fish farming, fish passage, crop production, reintroduction, spill, crossing, rising (sea levels), landslides, fracking, ash, eruption, pipeline, repositories, racing (of a storm). These are typically action or process nouns in an environmental, fisheries or energy context. The most negative tokens are the final subword of the process word ('-ling' in trawling = −10, 'blooms' −7, 'sal-in-ization' −6/−4).

L00_N1399_pos.wrong_label: Main signal. Fires on the verb token of a commander or ruler directing forces or subordinates, especially in historical or Chinese-historical war narratives. Examples: 'Cao Cao ordered…' (-7), 'Liu Zhang also sent troops' (-10, on 'sent'), 'Liu ordered continued monitoring' (-8), 'his men were marching' (-5). Weaker on 'Clinton may order' (military action), 'After leading the nation's…', 'the man who led them', 'Sherwood commanded the battalion', 'God orders Noah', 'leader Xi Jinping', 'will lead the Cowboys' (about -2 to -3). The activation sits on the verb itself: ordered, sent, marching, commanded, led. The noun after it ('troops') gets only a small value.

L00_N2419_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the first word of a proper place or street name, especially a modifier that opens a street, district, or area name. Strongest after a street number or a locative preposition (on/along/around the/in). Typical carriers are directional words like N, E., W, East, the period after 'E.', and modifiers like Old, Main, Lower, Upper. Examples: '157 N Old Carriage Road' (Old +10, N +5); 'located on 2145 Old Union Road' (Old +9); 'around the Old Course' (Old +9); '210 E. Grand' (E +7, '.' +9); '222 East Broadway' (East +8); 'Lower Nazareth Township' (Lower +6); 'Main Stage' (+7); 'the main street' (+7); 'Phuket's old neighbourhood' (+8); 'the old Town' and 'the old city wall' (+6–7). Street-number digits just before the name get +1 to +5 and rise toward the name. The preceding 'on/along/the' gets +1 to +3. Words after the modifier ('Road', 'Town', 'Township') get about +1 to +3. Weaker on generic 'main/city/town' in location contexts: 'main lounge' +3, 'city centre' +3, 'Denver West' +2, 'North Shore' +2.

L00_N2496_neg.wrong_label: The same kind of fragment token, but where the expected continuation is 'it' followed by a longer Latinate suffix chain ('-itable', '-ited', '-itician', '-itarian', '-itously', '-iting', '-itting', '-ithecus', '-it' as in merit/pundit). Examples: hosp|itable (-5), aud|ited (-5 to -3), -pol|itician / pol|itics (-5 to -4), Author|itarian (-5), precip|itously (-7), Austral|op|ithecus (-5), jan|itresses (-5), P|und|it (-4), relaxed-f|itting (-4), inc|iting (-3), Mer|it (-3). Also: Can|aan (-5) and Devanagari/Sanskrit fragment bytes (-10 in an Indic transliteration list).

L00_N2653_neg.wrong_label: Text about web links and browser windows opening: the phrase "will open in a new window" peaks on "in"/"a" (+9 to +10), with "open" around +5 and "new"/"window" +2 to +4. Related link/HTML boilerplate also fires: "(new windows)" (+5), "click the link to open it" (it +4), <a href="" title=""> (a +4), href="https://example.com/" (+5), "links on this website to other websites" (+2 to +3), "third-party website", "paste onto your website or blog" (+2 to +3). A weaker generalization covers physical openings and closures: roll-up or roll-off doors (roll/up/- +3), portcullis (+3), barn doors, sash, trim and door lists (commas/"and" +2 to +3), window mullions/lancets (+2 to +3), port-a-cot (+4), "empty cereal boxes" (+4).

L00_N2653_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that name or refer to social media as a category or a specific platform, fired on the naming token itself. Examples: 'social media', 'Twitter', 'Instagram', 'microblogs', 'Google+', 'foaf'. It is strongest when the platform reference is being anticipated, as in 'other social media', 'major social media', 'Weibo and other [microblogs', 'connect with us on'. Related weaker contexts also fire: user/follower/profile/feed words, posting activity, and 'Twitter' in share counters. One odd case: a year inside a Twitter or social-media history context ('in 2010', '2015') can reach about +5 to +7.

L00_N3027_pos.wrong_label: Digits of a year in a date stamp or metadata field such as 'Date:', 'Posted on', 'Uploaded:', 'Issue Date:', 'last updated on', or a publication year in parentheses. The peak falls on the last digit of the 4-digit year (the '4' in 2004, the '2' in 2022). The preceding year digits get small activations (+1 to +2). The hyphen or slash right after the year gets +2 to +4, and the following month digits get about +1. The effect is strongest in ISO-style YYYY-MM-DD dates that follow a label. Day or month tokens get weaker activation: '5/5 (Sunday, 16 December' gives +3, 'Oct' gives +3, and a leading '04-' gives +3.

L00_N3206_neg.wrong_label: The first digits (and leading space) of a number that is the primary value directly after a label or operator: 'Frac part = (0.62', 'added: 2012', 'apartments: 112', 'Sum of prime factors: 1215', 'main city beach: 600m', '3 - 02:37', '1872 - 1944'. Also fires on joining operators between quantities, such as '+' in '3.99 + free shipping', 'x' multipliers, '5+', and 'for every'. The activation sits on the space or digit just after ':', '=', '-', or '+'. Weak positive (~+1) appears on scattered tokens in names, addresses and titles.

L00_N3206_pos.wrong_label: Sharp, isolated dips on specific science-word tokens, mostly the prefix or first piece of a compound term. Examples: 'micro' -3 / '-' -8 in micro-organisms, 'bio' -4/-5 (biofilm, biofuel, bio-row), 'carbon' -3/-4 in 'carbon dioxide', 'ethylene' -4, 'angiotens' -4, '-' in physico-chemistry -5. Also ', ' separators in all-caps keyword lists (-3 to -5) and 'immuno' -5. In ordinary narrative or news text there is a mild -1 background on many tokens.

L00_N3975_neg.wrong_label: Tokens in computing/software/digital-technology contexts, especially noun phrases describing software, storage, memory or hardware. The strongest case is the patent-claim boilerplate 'The computer-readable storage medium of claim…', where the peak falls on '-readable' (+10). Nearby tokens are also high: 'computer' (+6), 'storage'/'medium' (+7), 'The' (+4), 'of' (+3), and the claim number/period (+2). Weaker hits: 'software' in 'software-based' or 'software stored in' (+2 to +3), 'memory' or 'heap' when discussing programming (+1 to +2), and 'GPU', 'Implementation', 'machines', 'programming', 'Internet', 'file on his computer' (about +1).

L00_N3975_pos.wrong_label: Tokens in the first sentence or clause of a fresh piece of prose that comes right after boilerplate such as a header, address, dateline, byline, citation or title. This is the expository, encyclopedic or promotional 'topic sentence' that introduces what the text is about. The activation peaks a few tokens in, on the main verb or predicate head and its first complement, then decays across the clause. Examples: 'Strip| away|+7'; 'Maritime archaeology| deals|+5 with|+4'; 'Today|+7,'; 'Animal lovers|+7 from'; 'is dedicated|+7 to|+3'; 'is making its mark|+7'; 'The|+7 qualitative exploration of|+5'; 'As a young child we|+7 dug'; 'mission of the ... Office is to fulfill|+7'; 'aims to provide a safe working environment|+6'; 'was raised|+6 by'; 'gives|+6 you the power|+4'; 'Spring is|+6 such|+5'; 'Ford Gallery is a|+6 contemporary art gallery|+4 in|+5'. A weaker version fires on descriptive or definitional predicate content elsewhere: 'X is/are...', 'of', 'for', 'to', abstract nouns like 'omnipresence|+6', 'hurtful|+6', '-esque|+6', 'rates|+5 ... have|+6'.

L00_N4111_neg.wrong_label: Content tokens inside Title-Case headings, product or service listings, and multi-token proper names or technical terms, often word-internal pieces. Examples: "D|Phil" −8; "Laser Vag|inal" −6; "Inade|qu|ately" −6; "Making The Decision To Undergo Vasectomy" ("go" −5); "Methods of| Losing Water Weight" −5; "Neighborhoods Act|ively Prepare" −5; "N|uestra" −5; "El| Segundo" −5; "Akashic Records/Psychic" −4 to −5; "Thor|acic" −4; "Div|ina" −5; a bullet "*" starting a list item −5. Explicit-content captions in Title Case also go negative.

L00_N4403_pos.wrong_label: Tokens where the next word is likely 'spirit/spirits' (or a near synonym such as soul, essence, ghost), usually the determiner or adjective just before it. Examples: 'encapsulate «the» spirit' (-10), 'awaken «that» spirit' (-9), 'symbolizes the «collective» strength, spirit' (-9), 'sends «the» spirits off' (-9), 'festive spirit' (-7), 'artisanal spirit' (-6), 'wine, beer «and» spirits' (-5), 'soul, flesh «and» skeleton' (-8), 'witches «or» devils' (-7). It also fires in Chinese and Korean contexts about ghosts or souls. Weaker negatives (-3 to -1) appear on related abstract virtue/collaboration phrasing: 'the collaborative approach', 'foster', 'grow in their faith'.

L00_N4590_pos.wrong_label: Statements about what can be built, produced, regenerated or redone, usually in software, build or fabrication contexts. Examples: "recompiled in a stable environment", "edit them to remove… and re-", "you can build them via knobs", "…voila… you get a dataset", "run it against different configurations", "can also be uploaded", "easier to slice as everything is done", "capable of printing up to", "pre-cut a 3D model in hundreds of shards in seconds", "customers will be able to have their name", "recording directly to executable test". The peak falls on the re- prefix, the outcome pronoun ('you' get, 'it' against), modal or infinitive words ('be', 'to', 'of', 'in') before the produced result or quantity, and on build/slice/done verbs. Words about 3D printing or printing often sit around −1 to −4.

L00_N4965_neg.wrong_label: Strong. Tokens naming the Jewish people or Israel, and Jewish religious figures or groups, in biblical, New Testament, or Jewish-Christian religious contexts. Peak examples: 'Israel' in 'glory to your people Israel' (-10); 'Jews' in 'Most Jews' (-10); 'Jews alone' (-8); 'Jewish' in 'Jewish State' and 'Most spiritual traditions, Jewish' (-6 to -8); 'priests' and 'scribes' in 'chief priests with the scribes' (-9); 'Pharisees' (-5); 'messiah' in 'the promised messiah' (-5 to -6); 'prophets' (-5); 'fulfillment' (-5). Scripture citations such as 'Isa.' (-5) and 'Ps' (-3), and 'Psalm' (-4), also fire. 'Priestly', 'chosen people', and 'waiting for him' give about -4 to -6. Surrounding tokens in Gospel or Psalm-like prose carry diffuse -1 to -2: 'the', 'of', 'your', 'his', 'Jerusalem', 'Olives'.

L00_N5232_pos.wrong_label: Subword tokens inside Russian/Ukrainian/post-Soviet proper names, mostly surnames, places and organizations. Examples: Voloshyn (osh +10), Turchinov (urch +7), Gorno-Altaisk (orno +6), Moskovsky, Dynamo, PJSC, OOO, Glushakov, Ovechkin, Fedorchuk, Rodchenko. The strongest token is a medial syllable of the surname, such as osh, urch, ch or ush, or the first token of the name. It also fires on the token right before such a name when a Slavic name is expected, e.g. 'on' before Moskovsky (+7), 'hosts' before Copenhagen in a Crvena Zvezda sentence (+7), or the comma before Oleh. There is weaker spillover to sports-report names (Koscielny +4, Connor +4, 'defeated' +5) and to function words in Eastern-European news contexts ('in the county' +5, 'attack on' +3).

L00_N5340_neg.wrong_label: Strong (to -10). Fires on passive or participial creation verbs that describe how or where an artifact was produced. The main trigger is 'made' used as a past participle after a noun: 'card made for', 'sauce made from', 'products made for people', 'movie made on a shoestring', 'rings made in'. Similar participles also fire: built, created, produced, crafted, designed, developed, collected. The negative also lands on the provenance tokens that follow: 'specially', 'In' (as in 'Made In India'), 'out of', 'for', 'with', 'from'. A further trigger is a made object in 'make a small boat out of' and 'made it just for you', where the negative falls on 'boat', 'out', 'it', and 'just'.

L00_N6256_pos.wrong_label: Continuation or suffix subtokens that complete a Latin word, mostly in the same contexts. Examples: 'hend|rer|it' (-4.5), 'temp|us' (-3), 'La|ude' (-3), 'la|ore', 'sapi|en', 'leo'. Endings of Latin-derived names also go negative: 'Corpus Christ|i' (-2), 'De|i', 'vom|itum', 'di|em', 'Terr|ae', 'Viv|it', 'Sav|itsch' (-1 to -2).

L00_N7327_pos.wrong_label: Academic, literary or humanistic evaluative phrasing about a work giving insight into a subject. Typical frames are 'of first importance in dealing with', 'an amazing insight into', 'a valuable lesson in', 'a view of', 'glimpse into', 'commentary on', 'hereinafter referred to as', and 'medieval history'. The activation lands on prepositions and function words that link the work to its subject ('into', 'with', 'in', 'of', 'as', commas). Typical values are -1 to -3; the peak is -7 on 'with' in 'dealing with'.

L00_N7669_pos.wrong_label: Very weak, at most about -1. It shows up on tokens just before a small count or value in boilerplate: 'All times are GMT -4', 'The following 33 pages', 'Page 1 of 2', and on colons in metadata lines such as 'Date posted:', 'Difficulty:' and 'located in this country:'.

L00_N7950_neg.wrong_label: Conversational expressions of not knowing or discovery, mostly in dialogue or casual Q&A right after a question: 'I don't know', 'don't care', 'don't want', 'find out', 'Find out the answers', 'Oh'. The negative values fall on 'don't/'t', 'know', 'find', 'out', 'you', and 'I'.

L00_N7988_neg.wrong_label: Running imperative or descriptive text in recipe method steps and retail product descriptions. The neuron builds up across a sentence and peaks on function words that continue an instruction, such as "to", "for", "and", "," and ".". Examples: "bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook al dente, according to" (+10 on "to"); "Cook shells according to package directions" (+8, +7); "Let stand 10 minutes"; "rest, covered for 10 minutes"; "Cool on cooling rack 20 minutes". In fashion and home copy: "roll up the sleeves for summer", "makes it a stylish choice", "will give your little one", "to dress things up", "that you can do everything" (+3 to +7).

L00_N7988_pos.wrong_label:
The word 'top', or what comes right before it, used for rank or spatial position.
(1) Ranking 'top N' / 'Top List': 'Top 10', 'top-10', 'Top 20', 'ranks among the Top 5', 'we have rounded up the 10 best'. The negative value sits on 'top', the space, and the digits (-4 to -7), and also on 'the' just before (-5 to -8).
(2) Spatial 'on top': 'chocolate layer on top', 'place the cheeses on top'. Here the peak falls on 'on' (-8 to -10) and the preceding noun is also negative (-3 to -5).
(3) 'top' as a UI or physical part: 'top menu', 'the top reveals', 'top coat' (about -6).
(4) The idiom 'from the mountaintop': strongest on 'aint' (-8).
(5) Related superlative or ranking phrases, at -2 to -4: 'number one brand', 'top the list', 'outside the top three', a year range in a 'best films of 2000-2009' list.

L00_N8040_neg.wrong_label: Non-initial subword tokens inside rare foreign or exotic proper names and loanwords, usually tokens beginning with or ending a syllable on 'i': -ika, -ima, -iro, -ide, -iny, -ito, -ite, -izo, -ini, -ina, -imb, -itia, -ik, -iman, -ich, -idi. Examples: chit«ika», Brah«ima», Shuich«iro», Nik«ide», Ar«ima», Yak«ima», Akih«ito», chor«izo», Rim«ini». The activation sits on the fragment that continues the word, not on the first piece. Japanese, African, Italian, Indian and Sanskrit names are typical.

L00_N8146_pos.wrong_label: Mainly the first piece of a word that the tokenizer splits, when that piece is just the letter S or s (or N or n). Examples: 'S|emi-portable', 'S|avers', 'S|oul', 'Auto-S|cope', 'S|uck', 'non-s|ubsidized', 'S|unny', 'fence-s|itter', 'S|elenium', '*S|eltzer', 'N|INE', 'n|ixed', 'n|autical', '/s|ports'. These fire most when they start a new line or list item, or follow a hyphen or slash. A weaker second source is prose that compares attributes or lists benefits, often with high/low/less/more wording: 'switch to', 'such as', the commas in 'easier, faster', 'Lighter - Less', 'with much less', 'never goes above', 'range, extended'. In these, function words and list commas get +2 to +7.

L00_N8414_pos.wrong_label: Tokens completing a word or phrase that describes what something can be done with or how easily it can be used, especially in product or feature descriptions. Examples: 'searchable', 'usable', 'weldable', 'bendable', 'formable', 'towable', 'washable', 'doable', 'actionable', 'transferable', 'scrubbability'. Also the verb that ends an 'easy/free/simple-to-X' construction: 'free-to-use' fires on '-use'; 'easy to wear', 'easy to clean', 'simple-to-maintain' (fires on 'ain'), 'ready-to-serve', 'READY TO HANG', 'reader-friendly', 'hard to view'. The activation sits on the suffix or final verb token ('able', '-use', 'ain', 'searchable'), not on the 'easy/free' modifier.

L00_N8439_pos.wrong_label: Also word-start fragments, but different ones. Typical triggers are consonant-cluster onsets with r or l ('tr', 'Tr', '/tr', 'br', '-br', 'contr', 'Kl', 'Clo', 'Amb') plus 'pres', 'beh', 'Em', 'Ar', 'Yan' and 'oly'. Examples: Kl|out (-10), rattle-tr|aps, Tr|ance, /tr|acker, contr|aband (-6 to -7), re-br|anded, pres|cribes, beh|eld, Em|igsville, Clo|stridium (-6). Weaker cases (-3 to -4): contr|asts, e-br|ake, Amb|roise, proteoly|tically, Ar|abic, Yan|acocha. A function word after an odd noun phrase can also go negative, e.g. 'with' in 'external engines with' (-6).

L00_N9209_pos.wrong_label:
Fires on a content word that opens a slot the next words must fill. The activation sits on that word itself, not on the filler that follows. Main cases:
- Transitive or linking verbs and prepositions right before their object or complement: 'among' (the best), 'demonstrates', 'became'/'become'/'becoming' (a citizen, president), 'enables' (us to), 'justify', 'relates' (to), 'spent' (last night), 'spend', 'handle', 'involving', 'by' (Apple).
- Sentence-subject nouns just before their verb: 'bitcoin is', 'graduate, and', 'independent peer-run'.
- The close-paren of an enumeration marker at the start of a list item: '1)', '2)'. These reach about +5 to +6.
Weaker hits: nouns that introduce a following 'of'/'to' phrase ('example' of, 'implications', 'plug' of, 'heat' demands), and the article 'a' in some predicate positions.

L00_N9223_neg.wrong_label: Very weak (about +1). It appears on the 'far' of 'as far as', on 'right'/'wrong' in 'X is right / I was wrong', on 'view' in 'point of view', on 'questions' in 'with any questions you may have', and on 'date'/'updated' in 'kept up to date'. These are mostly scope or perspective framing expressions. Positive values essentially never go above about +1.

L04_N0384_pos.wrong_label:
Fires on tokens inside run-together lists or fragments of proper names, mainly personal names and surnames, often with no commas. Examples:
- baseball rosters: «Francis» -7, «Bryan» -10, Hudson/Santana -3
- personal names: Corbin «Jane» -7, HLB Mann J«udd» -7, Draya «Michele» -6
- band and artist names: Martin Medeski «Wood» -6
- obscure place names: «Po»cono -8, Misibis «bay» -7
- unpunctuated item lists: tea tree «clo»ve -8
Spam-like keyword strings and SEO strings also fire, e.g. Deals of the Day«more» -6, fisher price «easy» -6, Business «Development» -6 in a jargon list.

L04_N0606_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token 'instruction' used as a noun. This covers teaching or education ('step-by-step instruction', 'Math and ELA instruction', 'unique instruction in a specialized field') and directive senses ('a written instruction', 'follow one simple instruction', 'adverse inference instruction', 'instruction from the government'). The singular form fires strongest (+7 to +10). The plural 'instructions'/'Instructions' fires moderately (+3 to +5), for example 'care instructions', 'Special instructions for seller', 'in-game instructions'. Capitalized 'Instruction' in titles also fires (+7 to +8).

L04_N0606_pos.wrong_label:
Technical, software-oriented text where a program, application, script, app, website, server, renderer or other automated system is the subject or agent doing something. The neuron fires on the agent noun itself ("applications", "script", "website", "program", "websites") or on the verb/infinitive right after it that names what it does ("to access", "to use", "is giving", "is performing", "moves on", "set", "completed", "can't add", "would need to"). The strongest cases are where such software is framed as the user or actor of something:
- "send email from their applications" (+10)
- "renderers to access the data" (+9)
- "AR apps to use it" (+6)
- "no installer in the script" (+6)
- "The script is giving you" (+5)
- "a method is performing" (+5)
- "servlet moves on" (+5)
- "email from their website" (+5)
The same applies, more weakly, to non-software organizations or services acting as agents ("the service that performs payments can't add", "other companies ... set").

L04_N1124_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the time-unit noun of a past-time offset phrase, in narrative text where an event happened some span before the reference point. Typical forms are 'two years prior', 'eight years ago', 'a few weeks ago', 'less than two months earlier', 'just weeks before' and 'had been on a conference call earlier'. The strongest value lands on the unit word ('years', 'months', 'weeks'). It also fires on 'earlier' or 'in' when 'earlier' itself is the offset. Related spots also fire: past-perfect or reported-clause contexts that set up backstory, such as 'asked me what I was doing there' (peaking on 'doing'), 'had brought them in front of', 'grateful to be', 'right away', and 'came' in 'X came to'.

L04_N1558_pos.wrong_label: Technical, metadata-like noun compounds from software, documentation, version-control or text-processing contexts. It fires on the head or second word of attribute and measurement terms: 'mutation score', 'word count', 'full-text', 'case sensitive', 'modified files', 'test coverage', 'File change date and time', 'Revision Changes Path', 'Changes.txt for 13 changes', 'comparison chart', 'ports in this commit are shown', 'highest-hit DSMs', 'XMLSpy', 'Plagiarism'. In changelog or commit listings it also fires on the newlines, '>' and numbers that follow the field-header words. Scattered weak firing appears on obscure proper-name subword pieces (Klo-ak, Lingue-e, aur-is, discord-ant) and on count/number field labels ('Member count', 'membership number', 'daily hits', '100%').

L04_N2686_neg.wrong_label: Language about a person assembling or customizing their own selection from an array of options. Typical phrases are 'build your own custom X', 'Create-Your-Own', 'selecting their food items', 'choosing from a broad range of', 'fill their plates', 'buffet', 'Pick & Mix', 'customize your character', 'design their dream X', and lists of toppings or fixings to choose from. Activation peaks on the possessive or 'own' in 'your/their own', on the selection verb ('build', 'choose', 'selecting', 'create'), on 'from' after 'choosing', and on 'buffet'. Commas inside lists of topping choices also fire.

L04_N2686_pos.wrong_label: The same kinds of contexts, with a different set of phrases. Financial and legal disclaimers: "Management's Discussion and Analysis of **Financial**" (-10, the strongest), "Analysis **of**" (-4), "registered trademarks **of** their respective owners" (-5), "actual results **may** vary" (-4). Copyright lines: "Copyright **©** 2018" (-4). Site-navigation menus: "Main Navigation," (-3 to -4). Fixed titles: "Picture **of** the Day", "Journal of Cosmetics, Dermatological **Science**". Registry IDs: "NL**4**149" (-6). Name fragments: Gen|o Smith (-5), P|io, Pan|aj|achel, Crist|ob|al, Giov|annon|i, Vickie Win|ans, "Musee **des** Beaux-Arts".

L04_N2844_neg.wrong_label: Mostly appears in formal, factual English that reads as translated or non-native (news briefs, press releases, corporate or product blurbs, often French, Russian or EU in origin). It fires on the determiners, prepositions and modifiers inside a noun phrase that is building toward a concrete technical or factual head noun. Activation ramps up across the phrase and peaks on the last modifier before the head. Examples: 'recipients of the first|+10 dose'; 'financing of this wind power|+7 project'; 'Intensive Lightening|+7 Serum'; 'is on her next|+6 destination'; 'containers of mixed|+6 products'; 'an antioxidant|+6'; 'Genzyme, a Sanofi|+6 company'; 'in the|+6 south'; 'Its|+6 manufacturing|+5 areas'; 'France's|+6 Carrefour'; 'diuretic|+5 function'; 'in|+5 stock'; 'in|+5 private collections'. Common pattern: 'of/in/for the|+4–6' followed by an adjective or noun-modifier that peaks. The head noun itself is usually lower, around +1 to +2.

L04_N3130_neg.wrong_label:
Fires where expository body text begins right after a heading, title, product name or 'About X' / 'What is X?' line. The model is about to describe or introduce the named entity. The activation lands mostly on the newline that ends the heading ("Friday Night Funkin?
" +10, "About 8point3 Energy Partners
" +9, "About Bombardier Transportation
" +6, "Information about Avianna.
" +9). It also lands on the first word of the description paragraph, usually 'The' ("
The Beaver" +8, "
The past few weeks" +7, "
The front bedroom" +6). A related case is a phrase that announces what the content covers, on the preposition or verb introducing the topic: "Learn more about" +9, "introduction to using the Web API" +7/+5/+4, "Four images from a…" +7, "How to remove" +7, "With the second wave of the H1N1" +7, "let's see what features" +4. Heading-like questions ("What is X?", "What in the World is…") build up: 'What' +2–3, 'Is' +6, then a peak at the '?
'.

L04_N3130_pos.wrong_label:
Strong and rare. It fires on the first content token that starts a new segment right after a run of numeric or metadata material: timestamps, long numbers, hashes, prices or IDs, usually just after a newline. Examples:
- ">" quote marker after a timestamp: −7 to −10.
- "Listed" after a hex hash: −8.
- "|" table pipe after a number: −5 to −7.
- '"' after a number: −7.
- Words right after a year or zip code: "general" (−6), "Established" (−6), "can" (−5), "master call" (−4/−5), "Taxi" (−4), "Home" (−4), "Photo" (−3), "Date" (−3), "I" (−3).
The next one or two tokens after it decay to −1 to −3.

L04_N3524_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that come right before an expected word like 'alternative', 'option', 'substitute', 'choice', 'version', 'solution' or 'way'. These are mostly the adjective or determiner slot in front of that noun: 'a sensible [alternative]', 'humane [alternative]', 'cheaper [alternatives]', 'a good [substitute]', 'low-cost [options]', 'open-source [distribution]', 'The subsequent [choice]', 'debt-relief [alternatives]', 'as an [alternative]'. Also fires on 'search for [alternative]', 'look for new [markets]', and 'The [alternative]' after an alternative has been mentioned. The surrounding context is about replacing something: cheaper, better or different options, a turn to something else, or comparing choices.

L04_N3579_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that complete a statement of a benefit, saving or added amount. This is the resource or benefit word, or the preposition linking the amount to what it applies to. Examples: 'save a lot of TIME', 'labor SAVINGS', 'cost SAVING measures', 'efficiency GAINED in', 'Performance GAIN', 'adds ... half mile TO the hike', 'added about [number]', '$200,000 ON its energy bill', '40 million gallons OF water', 'hundreds of man HOURS and', 'saving ... money OVER other models', 'increased ... OVER the 44', 'won't lose much SPEED', 'immensely IMPROVE'. Common objects of saving are time, money, labor, productivity and efficiency. Activation builds across the phrase and peaks on the head noun ('time', 'savings', 'gain') or on the linking preposition after the quantity ('to', 'of', 'on', 'over'). Following conjunctions ('and', ',') often stay mildly positive (+2 to +4).

L04_N3579_pos.wrong_label: The dominant pole. Fires on short whole-word verb or function tokens that are German or Scandinavian, or that are English homographs of German words. Strongest is German ' ist' in German text: 'mehr ist' = -10. Other German finite verbs in German sentences: ' geht' -7, ' findet' -4, 'gt' / 'ht' verb endings -2, ' dass' -2, 'wann' -2. Swedish ' ska' gives -4. English homographs of German words are weaker: ' hat' (hatband) -3, ' war' (Iraq war) -3, ' muss'(ed) -2, ' hast'(ened) -2, ' will' -1 to -2, ' is' -1 to -2, ' men' -2. Word-internal 'ist' gives -2 when it begins a Germanic-looking stem: und|ist|urbed, Sch|ist|osomiasis.

L04_N4087_neg.wrong_label: Fires on a token that opens or sits mid-way through a familiar multi-token unit whose continuation is strongly predictable. Main cases: the first or middle part of a person's name, especially before an initial or before a surname split into pieces ("Mary| J|." Blige +7/+5, "Ron| Rosen"baum +7, "Rebecca J." +5, "Marie-J"ose +4, "Mary D." +4, "Mary" Beth +3, "Ernest Ar"isca +3); fixed phrases ("Roe v." +4); boilerplate web templates ("see what your friends| are| up to" with +4 on "are", "Ad blocker interference detected" +3 on "interference", "Displaying review 1" +4, URL path pieces like /News +4). The top activation (+10) is on the Chinese word 群众 inside a 庆…群众大会 (celebration mass rally) heading. Content words beginning stock collocations also fire ("integrates knowledge and theory" +5, "Short Film Screenings" +6, "An obituary is not available" +5 on "is").

L04_N4122_neg.wrong_label: Tokens in non-English running text or non-Latin scripts, especially the first byte or token of a multibyte character or a new foreign word. Examples: Bengali, Devanagari and Greek characters, a stray byte before a number, and Dutch, Danish/Norwegian and Italian words or suffixes (-elijk, -izzazione, delle, volte, een, jeg). Also Cyrillic/Latin homoglyph spam (Үоu). The strongest values come right after an English context switches into a foreign script.

L04_N4122_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the head itself: the noun or pronoun that refers back to an already-established entity, especially as subject or object inside a clause. Examples: "sending|them" (=friends) -10, "the velocity|vector" -10/-6, "in|my" -10, "per migrant|worker" -9, "coached by|him since|they|were" -4/-8/-4, "the|child|'s" -8, "the|parameter" -8, "PNL|is|the" -7/-4, "single grits,|tool" -7, "When|he" -7, "which|he", "which|has" -6.

L04_N4152_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token immediately BEFORE an expected word-internal 'log'/'logs' fragment, i.e. when the current token is a prefix that 'log' will complete. Examples: 'c' before 'logged' or 'logs' (+10, +5), 'web' before 'logs' (+9), 'back' before 'logs' (+7), 'CO' before 'LOGNE' (+5), 'PHARMACO' before 'LOGY' (+4). It also fires on similar ambiguous word-starting fragments that could continue that way, such as 'sp' in spammers/spidery (+6/+7), '-c' in self-cleaning (+5), '|c' in cottage (+6), 'Techn' (+5), 'R' in Rival (+5) and '-s' in foot-soldiers (+5). The activation sits on the prefix token, not on 'log' itself; 'log' itself is only about +1.

L04_N4424_pos.wrong_label: Number tokens in repetitive, structured lists of dates, times, figures or stats, such as timestamp lines, news-feed dates, rankings with values, percentages, age lists and dimensions. The model is predicting the next digits. Activation lands on the digit or punctuation tokens inside the number, especially the leading digit after a space and the '0' in '20xx' years. It also lands on separators (',' ':' '-' 'x' '.') and on the month or weekday token that starts a repeated date entry. It is strongest when the same format has already appeared earlier, so the second and third entries in a list fire more than the first.

L04_N4446_neg.wrong_label: Words that mark the next step in a cause→effect chain, where a consequence follows from what was just stated. The strongest tokens are the connective adverbs themselves: 'turn' in 'in turn' (+6 to +10), 'thus', 'therefore', 'consequently', 'hence', and 'consequ-/ent' as in 'consequent drug use'. Activation is highest in an explicit chain such as 'X means Y, which in turn means Z' or 'A, and thus B'. It spills over at lower levels onto nearby tokens: the preceding 'and', ',', 'which', 'in' (+1 to +3), and the following comma, 'means', or verb (+2 to +8, e.g. 'means' after 'in turn' was +8). Weaker cases include 'which means', 'which creates', 'bringing with it', arrows in a chain ('->' about +5), 'subsequently', 'associated', and the 'and' in '(and external SSDs)' that extends an implication.

L04_N4446_pos.wrong_label: Tokens specifying a time schedule, interval, starting point or progress milestone rather than an end condition. Examples: '.\n' after 'Turn it over after 12 hours' (−8), 'work' in 'it would work' (−7), 'every 5 min' ('min' −6, the space before the number −5), 'reach your' in 'until you reach your normal regimen' (−6), 'start at' (−4/−5), 'about 2 cups' (−5), 'save-and-resume' (−5), '3 days on, 3 days off' (−4), 'and then' (−4), 'by the time you retire' (−4), 'the event' (−4), 'stirring' (−4). The pattern is periodic or step timing and the onset or reaching of a state, rather than ceasing.

L04_N4466_neg.wrong_label: Tokens inside URLs, identifiers, citations and technical strings that come right after a domain or a known prefix, i.e. the next segment the model must 'complete'. Examples: path starts (/t, /j, /pages, /wiki, /app), country codes after .com (au), short-link TLDs (.to, .tt), 'protected' in [email protected], 'MESSAGE' in BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE, citation-year closers '(2001).', and ID suffixes such as ISRCTN. Weak positives (+1 to +2) also occur on the second subword of fragmented proper nouns or terms (OStatus, Salmon, ntfs-3g, all-purpose in recipes, cic-adas).

L04_N4466_pos.wrong_label: Text in archaic, King-James-style or liturgical/poetic register, especially second-person address to God or a listener. The strongest activations fall on the 'th' token beginning an archaic second-person pronoun: 'th' in thine/thou/th'. Examples: 'shall be th|ine' scores +9 to +10, 'blow th|ine enemies' +8, 'Th|ou goest' +9, and 'holier-than-th|ou' +10 (with '-than' at +5). Within such passages, function words and verbs carry moderate activation: that, shall, be, which, with, when, if, ',', 'Behold', 'unto', verbs with -eth or -est. Modern biblical or sermon quotes that address 'you' ('If you seek her', 'He shall baptize you', 'Humble yourselves... he will exalt you') give weaker activation, about +3 to +5, on the verb or conjunction just before the addressee.

L04_N5009_pos.wrong_label: Abundance or quantity constructions that introduce a plural or mass complement. The peak is on the linking preposition or the quantifier: 'teem(ing) with' (−7 to −8, on 'with'), 'a coating of', 'a large volume of', 'full field of', 'full complement of', 'wealth of' (−6/−7, on 'of'). The quantifier itself also carries negative values: 'large' (−3 to −6), 'many' (−6), 'contains no' (−6 on 'no'), 'has 3 grading games' (−6), 'vast amount of', 'various', 'entire nation', 'wide range of'. Activation is milder (−1 to −3) when the quantity phrase is generic, e.g. 'great selection of'.

L04_N5138_neg.wrong_label: Strong and dominant. It fires on the token 'damage' / 'Damage' / 'damages' / 'damaged', meaning physical or property harm. The strongest cases are compounds and insurance/restoration contexts: water damage, smoke damage, structural damage, storm damage, Concealed Damage, Natural Resource Damage, game stats like Two-Hand Damage. These reach -8 to -10. Related harm/loss nouns fire more weakly: 'loss' (-4 to -5, with a following 'of' at about -2), injury/Injury (-3 to -4), 'Dam' as the start of a name like Damian (-4). Faint spillover of about -1 lands on neighboring words (hurt, repair, restoration, Protector, Insurance, suffered).

L04_N5955_neg.wrong_label:
Noun-phrase continuations and heads in descriptive, list-like or web-UI boilerplate text that are not instructions. Examples:
- 'List »of« Westfall NPCs' (-10)
- 'See all »' and the newline after it (-9/-7)
- 'inside the »box«' (-9)
- 'News Feed or your »Timeline«' (-9)
- 'On Wed, 2…' email-quote headers (-9/-8)
- URL query parameters such as '&sr=', '&s=' (-6 to -9)
- 'a good amount »of«' (-8)
- 'lovers »and« haters' (-9)
- 'Electricity »poles«' (-9)
- 'boogie »shoes«' (-8)
- PHP '$select' (-8)
- the medal-list comma (-8)
Navigation links (See, List, Trending, Categories), sports narration, and dense URL or name strings produce many -1 to -5 values.

L04_N5955_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that set up a small, simple, innocent or unintended starting point which is about to be contrasted with a larger outcome. Examples: 'didn't mean to start cleaning—it just happened', 'What began as', 'a simple cough turns into', 'grow from strength to strength', 'founded as', 'starting small with only', 'originally imagined', 'initially one-man firm', 'start off simply enough,', 'from small beginnings as', 'began with just'. Activation lands on the beginning or minimizer word ('began', 'as', 'from', 'simply', 'initially', 'originally', 'small', 'just', 'ago') or on the punctuation/dash right after the setup clause, where the pivot ('it just happened', ', but', 'turns into') is expected.

L04_N6054_neg.wrong_label: The token "info"/"Info" (with or without leading space, also "-info") used as a standalone word meaning information: "more info", "any info", "Background info", "study.info", "Info Box", "Info Wars". Weaker firing (~3) on the subword "inf" when it starts a longer word (inf-requent, inf-idel, Z-inf-andel, inf-raction, inf-estation, inf-using, inf-illing), and ~5 on "Infos" (Infosys). Faint (~1) on related abbreviation-like stems such as "informative", "inform", "Prof", "intro", "summary".

L04_N6054_pos.wrong_label: Mid-phrase tokens of memorized multiword expressions or names, where the continuation is highly predictable. Examples: "Agree with manuscript results **and** conclusions" (+7); the middle subword of unusual proper names such as Faval|ora, Mont|el|iro, Mont|el|ukast, Gram|mer, Rip|ley, Rip|off Report, Wink|el|nk|em|per; "Centre **of** Excellence"; "Ligue **des** droits"; "Leo **di** Caprio". Also website-UI and policy boilerplate: "Privacy & Cookies Policy↵N|ecessary", "By screening submissions, **we**", "you may set **your** browser", "keyboard shortcuts**:**", "navigate to login.↵", "dialog window**.**".

L04_N6238_neg.wrong_label: Birthday and age-milestone contexts. The strongest case is the 'X turned 42 on April 8,' construction, where the peak (~10) lands on 'on' after the age number. The date pieces that follow get +3 to +6: the month name, the space before the day digits, and the comma. The space before the age number gets ~+5. The word 'birthday'/'Birthday'/'birthdays' fires reliably at +4 to +7 (e.g. 'my birthday', 'Happy Birthday', 'birthday party', 'birthday wishes', 'birthday cake'). The word after it often continues: 'boy' +6, 'wishes' +6, 'for' +4, 'party' +2, 'parties' +1. Weaker cases (+1 to +4) include turning or reaching an age: 'turns 30 two days', 'will turn 17 this year', 'will be one year in a few days', '300th'. Birth dates ('born on August 28') reach ~+3 on the date digits.

L04_N6984_neg.wrong_label: Number or ordinal words, and the noun or hyphenated piece right after them, when the number is a compound or attributive modifier specifying a unit, instance or size. Examples: 'one-day visits', 'first license', 'second year', 'two-bedroom', '1-bedroom', 'first dose', 'third day', 'three-dose', 'part-time', 'first time', 'an acre of'. The peak lands on the number/ordinal word itself ('one' −10, 'first' −8, 'second' −6, 'third' −5) or on the hyphenated unit noun ('-bedroom' −5/−6), with spillover of −1 to −4 on the next noun ('visits', 'year', 'dose'). Weaker negatives appear on 'partially', 'fully', 'no plans', and '0' digits in money amounts like £100,000.

L04_N6984_pos.wrong_label: Page-number contexts in bibliographic citations and metadata. The strongest firing is on the first digit after 'page' (e.g. 'page 1' gives +10). Strong firing also lands on the dash or en-dash in page ranges ('91–98', '43-7', '109-122'), at +4 to +9, and on the digits after that dash, at +2 to +7. Weaker firing hits 'Pages:', 'Number of Pages in PDF File:', 'Page Range:', 'pp.', 'Page 1 of 2', 'pg.1' and 'Article number:', at +2 to +9 on the colon or 'of' and on the following digits.

L04_N7042_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token BEFORE an expected standalone word 'log', 'login', 'log in', 'log out', 'logging', 'changelog' or 'Logos' in computing or account contexts. This is usually a verb slot: '->' before 'log out' (−7), 'must' before 'log it' (−5), 'to' or 'you' before 'login'/'Log In'/'Access' (−4 to −5), 'server' or 'audit' before 'log' (−3/−4), 'chang' before 'elog/elist' (−3/−4), 'Channel' before 'Logos' (−4). Weaker negatives (−1 to −3) appear on nearby function words in login/password/account instructions ('to', 'you', 'could', 'still').

L04_N7042_pos.wrong_label: The dominant pole. Fires strongly on the token "all" when it starts a spatial-dispersal idiom: "all over (it / the place / the world / the city / the US)", "all around (us / you)", "all round", "from all parts of the world". Magnitude peaks at "all" itself (-6 to -10). It is strongest when a concrete plural or mass noun, or a scattered-stuff verb or object, comes just before it: "stickers all over" -10, "fling it all over the place" -9, "sad faces all round" -8, "shops all over the city" -7, "oil all over" -7, "kitchens all over the world" -6, "lurk all around us" -6. The preceding noun or pronoun also often goes mildly negative (-1 to -4), e.g. "stickers" -3, "it" -3, "kitchens" -4. Following tokens such as "over", "round", "place", "world" get small negatives (-1). Weaker negatives (-1 to -4) appear on related distribution or extent contexts without "all": "exported to 60 countries or regions around the world", "protests and occupations around", "all day, all year" (-2/-3), "all the while" -3.

L04_N7491_neg.wrong_label: Physical extraction or removal phrasals, mainly the particle after the verb: 'dig out', 'dig up', 'pull out', 'dug out', 'suck out', 'flush out', 'pluck X out of', 'rip it out', 'tug out'. Weaker cases are insertion phrasals like 'put in', 'imbed into', 'stuck a tube in', 'ferrying cargo into'. The particle 'out'/'up'/'in' carries the peak, about +2 to +4. The next determiner or possessive ('the', 'your', 'his', 'our') and 'of' get +1 to +3. The verb itself ('dig', 'digging') gets about +1. Maximum observed positive is only about +4.

L04_N7491_pos.wrong_label: The preposition 'in' (sometimes 'to', 'over') right after an abstract noun naming a quality, achievement, gap, standard, direction or focus, where 'in' opens the domain or area it applies to. Examples: 'excellence in', 'standardisation in', 'flexibility in', 'gap in', 'directions in', 'consistency in', 'success in', 'lack of openness in', 'efficiency in mind', 'outstanding achievement in', 'track record in', 'frontiers in'. The preceding abstract noun often gets a small positive value (+1 to +2), and the token after 'in' sometimes gets about +1.

L04_N7508_neg.wrong_label: Affectionate physical embrace or holding: 'arms' in 'in my/her/his arms' or 'each other's arms', hug/hugs/hugged/hugging, embrace(s), 'arms open wide', bosom, 'hold you'. The strongest values fall on 'arms' and 'hug' forms. Weaker values go to love, picking someone up, and figurative 'embraces the notion' or 'all-embracing'.

L04_N7508_pos.wrong_label: Text that instructs or explains how a product or device is physically treated or operated. Typical cases are garment care labels ("Machine wash cold, gentle cycle, do not tumble dry", "wash at 40°", "pre-washed for softness"), device mechanisms ("uses ultrasonic technology to deliver a safe, heat-free mist", "the nicotine vaporizes the…", "turntable motor unit", "reads the very center") and step-by-step run/install directions ("run the exe application", "run the game as administrator as it helps prevent crashes", "burning the DSL image to a CD-R", "double-click", "running under OS 9"). Activation lands on the key process or condition words: washed, cold, spin, heat, 40, CD, vaporizes, run, administrator, and the 'it' in 'as it helps'. The function words that continue the instruction also fire (for, to, the, and).

L04_N7543_neg.wrong_label: Names of publishers, journals, venues and institutions inside academic citations and affiliations. The head or brand token carries the activation: 'Elsevier', 'Springer', 'Sciences' (EDP Sciences, Sciences Po), 'Proceedings', 'Workshop', 'Institute', 'Bulletin', 'Scientific' (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 'Cambridge', 'University', 'conference proceedings'. Nearby citation tokens are also negative: 'vol', 'Journal of', 'on', 'Techniques', 'Methods'.

L04_N7543_pos.wrong_label: The dominant pole. It fires on descriptions of muscular or facial movement, tension and relaxation, and posture: someone physically moving, tensing, or relaxing a body part, or a facial expression forming. The strongest token is the body part or muscle noun inside a movement or relaxation phrase, or the verb or preposition of the expression. Examples: "move your shoulder blades" (shoulder -10), "grinning from ear to ear" (ear -8), "smile tugged at" (tugged -8, at -7), "progressive muscle relaxation" (muscle -8), "twitch into a twisted smile" (a -7), "features are lifted" (-7), "release tension" (-6), "unwind your mid-section" (-5/-6), "knitted her brows" (-5), "eye corners" (-6), "facial expressions" (-4). It also responds to facial and neuromuscular conditions, e.g. "Bell's palsy" (palsy -10) and "headache" (-5).

L04_N8478_neg.wrong_label: Prepositions and connectives that introduce the variable or operating condition a quantity depends on or is measured under, usually in technical, scientific or automotive text. Examples: 'as a function OF the load', 'over AN extensive range OF', 'even AT HIGH volume', 'decreases AS it', 'WHEN equipped', 'increases WITH openness', 'regardless OF', 'depending ON', 'depends ON the number', 'independent of level OF', 'stable WITH respect', 'below 100 C', 'above 4500 rpm', 'at LOWER cost', 'gets better WITH age'. The activation sits on the preposition or connective (of/on/with/at/as/over/when/below/above) and spills onto the next 1–3 tokens, which are typically the condition itself (the/an/high/extensive/progressive, or digits of a threshold number).

L04_N8478_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the verb (often gerund or bare infinitive) naming an action or undertaking that a person or agent performs, in contexts that frame it as a task, process, or endeavor. Typical frames: 'how to implement', 'what it was like to live in', 'before entering this space', 'how to go about troubleshooting', 'Those using these images', 'interested in applying for', 'required for the auditor to deliver', 'what goes into making', 'carrying out research', 'the costs of renting', 'Passing this test', 'People who experience'. Clause- or sentence-initial gerunds/infinitives also fire ('Finding the best website', 'To create a new', 'Doing'). The peak sits on the main action verb. The framing words leading up to it (how/to/before/for/into/of) ramp up at +1 to +5. Particles or prepositions completing the phrasal verb can carry the peak too ('get your hands on' +9 on 'on', 'go about' +8, 'carrying out' +8). Weaker spillover follows on the object (this/one/a +1 to +4).

L04_N8913_neg.wrong_label: Commodity or industry words used as modifiers that name an economic sector, trade, or producer group. Typical cases: oil, coal, tea, steel, wine, glass, farm, mineral, vine, tire, and small (as in small business or small-scale). Seen in phrases like "oil sector engineer", "tea party activist", "small business owner", "coal mines", "domestic steel industry", "wine-making families", "Farmers and Greens", "Chamber of Commerce and Industries". Activation sits on the sector word itself, usually the modifier before the head noun (sector, company, industry, owner, mines). The following head noun (sector, business, mining) gets weak spillover. In 'Chamber of Commerce and Industries' and 'Farmers and Greens' the peak is on 'and', the conjunction linking sector/group names. Tea is strong even in tea tree oil.

L04_N8913_pos.wrong_label: Positive values come from content words in generic website chrome and boilerplate. Examples: ad-blocker notices ('disabling these ads|+10 blocker'), word-list/anagram pages ('in this word|+7 list'), H-Net notices ('submitted|+7 to us'), and forum or vBulletin footers ('Copyright', '-' in '2000 - 2016', 'vBulletin|+6'). Others: 'emailed to me|+6', 'this site has|+5 to offer', '24/7', 'Then|+5 you can start reading', 'Publisher:', 'members' in 'users browsing this thread', and 'other marks|+4 are trademarks'. The activation usually lands on the noun or verb completing a stock phrase: ads, word, submitted, me, has, Embed, bold.

L04_N9413_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the word completing a paired opposite-direction or reversible-action phrase: 'to and from', 'to/from', 'import and export', 'upload and download', 'pick-up' after drop-off, 'take off', 'enter or exit', 'up or down', 'attach/remove', 'convert between', 'dawn and dusk', 'back-and-forth to'. The peak is on the second directional term ('from', 'export', 'down', 'exit', '-up', 'off') or the linking conjunction just before it ('and', 'or'), especially when a first direction ('to', 'import', 'drop-off') came earlier. 'between' gets moderate activation when it means transfer or conversion between two things. Weaker activation spreads to the following noun ('course', 'airport', 'files', 'work').

L08_N0068_pos.wrong_label: Tokens naming or describing a process that runs over time and reaches completion, usually in instructional or technical text where a later step waits on it. Examples: software operations (export request, conversion, download, transfer, import, restore, booting, printing queue, installation), cooking steps that run until done (until dissolved, until liquid is absorbed, add eggs one at a time, sugar dissolves), and devices or other things running (water running, charging program, garage door closing). The strongest firing is on the process noun or the completion predicate inside 'once/after/when the X is finished/complete' and 'click Start to start the conversion' frames.

L08_N0791_pos.wrong_label: Single-token all-caps initialisms/acronyms, especially those beginning with P or C (PCR, PCB, PCA, PC/PCs, PVC, CPR, CDC, CQC, QC, GC, CD) plus DNA/mRNA. Activation sits on the acronym token itself, mostly when it is used as a noun or modifier in running text. PCR in a scientific methods context is strongest. A trailing piece such as 's' or 'R' after the main token gets a small spillover.

L08_N2092_neg.wrong_label: The second subword of 'fasten' forms: the 'en' or 'ened' token after 'fast' (fasten, fastened, fastenings), giving +5 to +9. Weaker hits, +3 to +5, come from 'dump/dumping/dumped' (on the dump token or the -ing token), 'Consulate' (the 'ate' token), 'devolve' ('olve'), 'bestowed', 'frowned', 'graffiti' (the 'iti' token) and 'Fitting'. Faint +1 to +2 responses appear on verbs of granting or accepting such as 'accepted', 'applicable', 'appoint', 'welcomed', 'vowed' and 'govern'. Roughly, the positive pole is the completing token of verbs about attaching, securing, disposing of or bestowing, with 'fasten' far the strongest.

L08_N2134_pos.wrong_label: The domain-name pieces of well-known site URLs, especially '.com'. The strongest case is the TLD right after a multi-piece subdomain such as 'diy.sndimg.com' (-10). Also negative: '.apple' in itunes.apple (-4/-5), huffingtonpost.com, time.com, diabetes.org, businessinsider.com (-2 to -4). Moderate negatives (about -3) fall on command and program names in shell or tech instructions (make, signtool, Plagger) and on the first path digit after a short path.

L08_N2461_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token for the word 'serious'/'seriously' and close synonyms of gravity, such as 'grave' and 'severe'. It fires most when they describe harm: injury, illness, side effects, risk, consequences or mistakes. The concept extends weakly to related severity or magnitude words: 'critical', 'Severity', 'fatal', 'catastrophic', 'major', 'significant', 'gross(ly)', 'death(ly)'. L08_N2461_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token 'rental' or 'rentals' in any sense of renting: property, equipment, cars, boats, dumpsters, bins, textbooks, goats, test-net rental, even sports 'rental players'. Related forms are weaker: 'renting' ~8, 'Rent/rent' (noun or verb) ~5-6, 'lease/leases/leasing' ~4-5, 'landlord' ~3, 'hire' (as in rental) ~2-3, 'apartment(s)' ~2. L08_N2661_neg.wrong_label: Short tokens, often capitalized, that are complete abbreviations or acronyms standing alone, where the word is finished rather than continuing. Examples: LR (living room) -6, SS (stainless steel) -4, PD/AD (diseases) -3 to -4, NC -4, OO (object-oriented) -4, cu. in. -4/-3, Ss (subjects) -4, PK -3, St. -3, Co. -3, pic -3, elec -3. Mild negatives (about -1) appear on some name or word fragments in ambiguous contexts.

L08_N2661_pos.wrong_label: Words that name the positive payoff, value or result of using something, in promotional or evaluative text. The main triggers are 'benefit(s)', 'advantage', 'save', 'solve', 'reduce/lower', 'realize (success)', 'results ... seen' and 'savings'. The peak lands on the payoff word itself. Activation is strongest when the context sets up an expectation of a benefit, as in 'what are the benefits of', 'the advantage of X is that', 'save up to 90%', 'more problems than they solve', 'further facilitate the above mentioned benefits' and 'can save money by'. Tokens right after the payoff word also get moderate activation, e.g. 'of', 'to', 'by', 'that', '%', the '?' after 'advantage'. So do framing words just before it, such as 'the', 'great', 'several', 'further', 'save up to'.

L08_N2740_neg.wrong_label: Two kinds of context. (1) Anatomy of blood vessels and circulation, peaking on the vessel noun: 'vascular bed' gives -10/-7, 'capillaries' about -5, 'blood vessels' about -4/-3, 'veins' -4, 'drainage' -3, 'circulation of blood' -3. (2) Document-structure headings of the 'PART 1:' / 'Part II:' / 'Part 2:' type, peaking on the numeral or colon at about -3 to -4. Some instructional sentence ends also fire weakly, e.g. 'described below.' about -3 and 'Viewing Abstracts.' about -3.

L08_N2740_pos.wrong_label: The word accredit-: the token "accredited", "accreditation", or the "credited" piece in "SC-accredited". It fires hardest in certification contexts such as "X is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission", "an accredited agency/provider/exercise physiologist", "LEED Accredited Professional" and "fully accredited". Words from neighboring credential or affiliation fields fire only weakly: the "portion" in apportion/malapportionment, "Impact factor", the "unct" in acupuncturist, AACN/ACC acronyms, and affiliated/affiliates.

L08_N3015_pos.wrong_label: Two kinds of token. (1) Word pieces inside romanized, often Japanese/Spanish-like proper names: 'TOYO' in a promo code ('YO' −10), 'Toyo' ('yo' −4), 'Soto' ('oto' −5), 'Yotsuya' ('uya' −3), 'Trewartha' ('rew' −3), 'trefoiled' ('tre' −3). (2) 'quality'/'qualities'/'literacy' used as a neutral property, measure or plural noun rather than as praise: 'three qualities' (−4), 'non-stick qualities' (−3), 'essential qualities' (−3), 'pursuit of quality' [of life] (−3), 'management of quality' [control] (−3), 'increased literacy' [rates] (−3), 'scenery' (−3). Small −1 values appear on 'zodiac', 'simple', 'courteous', 'facilities' and some name pieces such as 'Tyndall'.

L08_N4014_pos.wrong_label: The first token of a rare word that the tokenizer has split into pieces. These are mostly proper names (people, places, brands, institutions) and some uncommon common words. The activation sits on the word-initial fragment, before the rest of the word appears. Examples: Moiz «Sy»ed (+10), «W»adham College (+8), «Tar»bet, «Ch»orlton, «Ch»autauqua, «Ch»iswell, «Mer»iden, «T»avira, Zhou Xia«oh»u, Katie «Cru»ice, «Pro»enza Schouler, Alison «H»irst, «N»UI Maynooth (all ~+5 to +6). Common-word cases include «gr»inds, «gr»unge, «gr»ating, «gr»annish and white-lipped «pe»ccary (~+6). Weaker cases (+2 to +4): R«ic»ciardo, P«iz» Boè, «Ro»straver, «Du»Pont, «Tw»entekanaal, «Fest»ivals, Madeleine «H»inde, e-«br»ake. A preceding 'at'/'in'/'and' before the name sometimes gets +1. There is also a secondary positive response (+1 to +5) on scattered words in site-description boilerplate, e.g. comment-moderation text ('screening', 'informed', 'engage', 'aims').

L08_N4570_pos.wrong_label: Clause-level coordinating connectives that begin a new conjoined predicate or event, especially in sequential narration. The peak is on the second word of a sequence connective: 'and then' gives 'then' about +8 to +10 and 'and' about +3 to +6. Other second words behave the same way: 'and also' (+7), 'and not' (+8), 'and now', 'but rather' (+7). A bare 'and' or 'And' joining clauses or predicates is moderate, e.g. 'and died in', 'and to unmanaged', or a sentence-initial 'And' (+7/+8). 'and'/'or' joining noun phrases is weaker (+1 to +4). List bullets or numbers that start a new item ('•', '2.', '-') get +2 to +5.

L08_N4582_neg.wrong_label: Mostly in Christian church, liturgy or parish-bulletin text. It fires on function words and connectors that come right before a specific named item, place, event or term. Typical triggers are 'the', 'of', 'on', ':', opening quotes, and the first digit of a year or time. Examples: 'back down the center aisle to the [street end] of the' (the +7, of +2, the +5); 'Holy Eucharist, Rite II: A festive celebration… using the more contemporary language of' (+3 to +6); 'officially called "E[vangelii]' (" +3, E +4); 'known as the “sede vacante”' (+3); 'on the first Saturday of November' (the +5); 'celebrate the Res[urrection]' (+4); 'from 3:30 to 5:00' (the 0 in 5:00 gets +5); 'Page 4 June 13, 2005' (the space before 2005 gets +6). It also fires weakly on church-adjacent formal text such as addresses, product names, and ceremony programs ('playing of "Taps"').

L08_N4582_pos.wrong_label: Words for blogs and blogging content. Strongest is the '/blog' path segment in a URL (around -9 to -10). Next are 'posts' in 'blog posts' or 'wordpress posts' (-4 to -7), 'blog' (-3 to -7, and 'blog' used as a subdomain is about -5), and 'bloggers' (-7). 'author' or '-utors' as a word fragment, as in 'authorizing' or 'contributors', is about -6. Other negatives are milder: URL query parts like 'LinkId' (-5), '/fwlink' (-2), and 'articles' (-2). Brand or domain-name tokens just after 'www.' are often slightly negative, -1 to -3 (e.g. '.youtube', '.daily', 'post' in huffingtonpost). Occasional weak negatives (-1 to -3) hit 'BEGIN' in PGP headers, month names at the start of a line, and 'Girlfriend' in a headline list.

L08_N4651_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token right before an expected 'if'/'when' conditional or circumstance clause. Typical slots: the predicate in 'what happens [if]', 'don't be surprised [if]', 'would you be disappointed [if]', 'X gets erased [when]', 'occurs [when]', 'is curable [when]', 'contempt charges [if]', 'a problem [if]', 'everyone gasped [when]'. In each case the activating token completes a predicate whose natural continuation is a condition or trigger. Weaker cases are sentence-final periods in expository or technical prose that set up a 'When…/If…/Some…' follow-up sentence, e.g. '...(AMF) panel.' followed by 'When the mains power…'.

L08_N4651_pos.wrong_label: The first subword token of a proper name that the tokenizer splits into pieces. Typical cases are surnames and place names whose first piece looks like an ordinary word or prefix: Kathryn «Big»elow, Gary «Left»in, «Gl»encore, «Gl»endale, «Gl»ade, «Gl»yne, «Bar»bour, «Bar»row, «Bar»ose, «Col»lier, «Col»lopy, «Little»field, «South»field, Rod«denberry», «T»epic, «Ph»arr, Al«bag»hdady. The activation sits on the token where the name begins and its continuation is still unresolved. The 'Gl' onset is especially strong, and lowercase gl- words also fire («gl»owed, «gl»int). Weaker variants fire on the first digit of a number in an address or phone context, such as the area code «(4»09, a highway number «4»32, or the year 1«7»97. Commas and connectives inside lists of place names get small activation (+1 to +3), e.g. 'Littlefield, TX, …'.

L08_N5995_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the slot between a verb of putting on, taking off, covering or wearing and its object. It hits the possessive or article right after that verb or preposition, before the garment or covered thing: "takes off **her** bikini", "take off **my** gloves", "pull off **my** heavy boots", "removed **their** shirts", "throw on **a** cardi", "dressed **in** flashy jackets", "wearing **my** cutest outfit", "pulled **my** chair", "melted **the** snow", "cover with **your** thumb", "jeans in a **similar** hue". It sometimes extends to the modifier before the garment (heavy, flashy, smart) and to wristbands. The verb itself (off, on, wearing, dressed) is usually only about -1 to -3.

L08_N6218_neg.wrong_label: Fires inside acute-injury reports, mostly sports news, on the function words just before the injured body part or injury noun. Typical frames are 'out/forced off with a [strained] hamstring', 'after aggravating his strained right calf', 'injured his ankle', 'broke my leg', 'suffering a nasty gash', 'return from his hip issue' and 'must have been broken'. The peak lands on the determiner or possessive (a/his/my), on adjectives (strained, broken, sore, nasty) and on laterality words (right, left). It is weaker on with/after/from and on injury verbs. The injury noun itself (hamstring, concussion, leg) is usually low.

L08_N6218_pos.wrong_label: Digits (and the '$', '£', '(+' or ',' tokens) of a secondary, alternative, restated or derived quantity that follows a first figure. Typical triggers: 'or $22,000' (conversion/alternative price), 'Save £7.50', 'Save 20% ($0.50', '(+15/Level', '(24 y, 1 m, 18 d', 'yards or 3281', a parenthetical local time '(7:33 a', a currency conversion after '£43,000; $85', 'about 160', 'an average of one every 8', 'maximum +25'. The strongest values land on the first digit or currency symbol right after 'or', 'Save', '($' or '(', and fade over the following digits.

L08_N6273_pos.wrong_label: Very weak, only about +1. It fires on the first subword piece of a multi-token word that begins with a consonant plus 'u' or 'oo' sound but is not the prefix 'sub-'. Examples: 'sug' in sugary/sugared, 'dub' in dubbing, 'bub' in bubbling, 'sab' in sabers, 'So' in Soothing, 'ub' in Shubham. It is essentially a minor orthographic or phonetic echo of the 'sub' token.

L08_N6479_neg.wrong_label: Tokens inside coordinated lists and repeated parallel structures, usually the 2nd, 3rd or later items. It fires most on the last token of an item that mirrors an earlier item's form, and on the separator (comma, 'and', 'or') right after that item, which sets up another parallel item. Examples: 'English, French«,»' in a language list; 'red deer «and» pigs«,»'; 'a finch «or» canary'; 'Alcott«,» Annehurst«,» and'; '/home/username-two/xyz«.com»' after an identical first path; 'F – 5 would be the camera «sticker»' echoing 'the Dart board sticker'; '3 suit «game»'; 'Joel Ros«ario», 20-1' in a results list; 'Washington«,» D.C.' at the end of a list of companies and cities; 'other types of «businesses»'. The neuron rises as the parallelism builds up.

L08_N6479_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the predicate word right after a subject or auxiliary when it opens a construction that needs a complement, especially an infinitive or verb phrase. Strongest (+7 to +10): begin/began/begins (+ to/V-ing/object: 'you begin to daydream', 'I began looking'); 'yet' in 'has/have/is yet to' (~+8, then 'to' ~+1); 'upon' in '[season/weather] is upon us' and 'upon check-in' (~+8 to +9); 'wish' in 'wish (not) to' (~+8); 'herein' in 'information contained herein' (~+8). Moderate (+2 to +5): modal 'may' (often 'may be required', 'may not', 'may apply'), 'appear(s) to', 'those (of)' as in 'those of the pastor', 'remains' in 'X remains our...', 'bear the name', 'attempted', 'purchased'. Weak (+1 to +2): following 'to', 'be', 'not', 'perhaps', 'however', 'just', 'nor', 'therefore'. The activation sits on the verb or particle itself, not on the complement.

L08_N6734_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that grammatically link or complete a modifier and announce an upcoming head noun or noun phrase. These include possessive ’s/‘s after names ('Racing Point‘s', 'Franklin‘s', 'Hardwick’s'), 'of' in quantity or part phrases ('piece of', 'line of', 'pieces of', 'years of', 'quality of'), and adjectival or compound suffixes ('-related', '-sales', '-private', '-isation', 'diluted'). The same role in CJK text counts: Japanese 的な and katakana pieces, Chinese 的/的新, and Korean object particles 을/를/들을. Modifiers that sit right before a noun also count ('outdoor' table, 'self' parking, 'single and double' pulse, 'Eagle' Ford).

L08_N6734_pos.wrong_label: Fires in health, anatomy or product text about bones, joints and muscles as things to protect, treat or move, rather than an individual's acute injury. The strongest spots are the preposition, conjunction or article just before 'joint/bone/muscle', as in 'glucosamine for bone & joint health' (the 'for' and '&' tokens), 'injected into the joint' (into/the), 'muscle and joint pain', 'my bones and joints', 'help bones and muscles develop', 'fold at the joints', 'cut off at the hip joint', 'surfaces of the facet joints', 'pain in the arms' and 'old bones'. L08_N6996_neg.wrong_label: Sparse, high values on the first piece of a word that the tokenizer has split, at the point where the model must supply a specific continuation piece. The activation sits on the opening fragment, not on the completion: 'sk' (skinned/skis/skews), 'be' (beading/BEINGS), '/ne' (neutered), 'K' (Kola), 'L' (Louboutin), 'H' (H&M), 'MON' (MONDAY), 'mon' (monamon), 'Garn' (Garni), 'N'/'endor' (Nendoroid). Weak positives (+1 to +3) fall on assorted function tokens: '(', '-', newline before a list item, and '1' starting a year such as 1961.

L08_N6996_pos.wrong_label: Nouns that name a media format, production unit, or entertainment product, especially 'video(s)'. Other examples: 'finale', 'pilot', 'cut' (as in a film cut), 'premieres', 'shorts', 'audio', 'acoustic', 'broadcasting', 'cover', 'entree', and 'Dramat' in 'Dramatists'. The activation lands on the format noun itself, usually after descriptors such as 'top comedy videos', 'directed video', 'new cut', or 'audio productions'. The neuron also fires weakly (+1 to +2) on related entertainment words such as drama, comedy, documentary, theatrical, premiered, Blu-ray, playwright, Hardcore and length.

L08_N7831_neg.wrong_label: Short symbol-like or odd-character tokens that come right after a number or code fragment, chiefly measurement and unit marks. The clearest cases are degree, foot and inch marks after digits: 52°, 19'2", 5’3”, 12" x 4", 40°. Others are currency or unit symbols in price lists or tables: € in a table, Kč (č), zł (ł), a garbled ¥ (Ę), µ. Also short tokens that open an identifier or a new item: the mask ∗ in kr∗∗∗@, Z in a timestamp 00Z, ®, the Q in iQ, 'IQ' as a formula term, 'ue' in ue_t0, 'Mix' after a line break, a CJK character starting a lyric line, characters inside URL query strings (?v=YU4DkH7). Magnitude is highest when the symbol directly follows a digit or a masked/structured string.

L08_N7831_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that express division into parts, ratios, or per-unit quantities inside numeric or measurement expressions: 'equal' in 'six equal pieces' (-10), 'pieces' (-5), 'one side' in 'length of one side' (-5/-7), the '/' in 'C/10' (-7), ')x' in a probability formula (-8), digits within arithmetic (-2 to -3), 'management fee' (-6), 'at least' for spacing (-5), 'biax' (-5). Also scattered tokens such as currency or units right after numbers ('€' -5, '2p.' -5, '500' -5, 'mW' -3, 'slender' -4, 'shown' -5). The common thread is quantification or partitioning of amounts, not named physical quantities.

L08_N8121_neg.wrong_label:

L08_N8143_neg.wrong_label: Nouns naming static physical features of water bodies and terrain in geographic or environmental text: 'surface' (ocean, Earth, water surface), river 'bank'/'bed', 'water' (shallow water, Intracoastal Waterway, waterfalls), 'floor', 'rock', 'soil', 'land', 'Floods' (as a named geologic event), coal 'bed'. 'water' tokens usually get +1 to +3.

L08_N8143_pos.wrong_label: Fires mainly in archaic, KJV-style or legalistic narrative prose. Examples: 'And that' in an old legal document (-10); 'him that is thirsty' (-6); ', and' before a verb or subject in biblical narrative (-3 to -4, e.g. 'surely redeem, and', 'sent, and fetched', 'arose, and her damsels'). L08_N8154_pos.wrong_label: Rare and hard to pin down from the examples. The windows that reach +10 show no marked token, so the peak probably falls at or near the end of the window. L08_N8214_neg.wrong_label: Fires on a token inside a familiar, formulaic phrase when the next word is strongly predictable from the phrase pattern. Examples: partitives and quantifier frames like "one| of", "some| of", "the kind| of", "sorts| of", "the daughter| of", "the number| of", "increase in the number"; idioms and proverbs like "When the going gets| tough, the| tough", "there| is always tomorrow", "let| go", "let their body rest", "diving into|", "What if I tell| you"; set constructions like "there had| been", "(there| were)", "Besides|,"; acronym expansions like "Girl Raised In| The South". L08_N8214_pos.wrong_label: Mainly the word 'If'/'IF'/'if' when it starts a sentence, quote, or list item, or appears as a capitalized acronym or name-like token.
