L08_N8299_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the first subword piece of an ordinary lowercase English common word that is split into pieces, where the model has to finish a known word. Examples are «l»ull, «l»ighthearted, «l»uster, anti-«de»pressants, ever-«d»ynamic, «hy»dropower, self-«e»vident, «unin»formed, un«ap»ologetic, well-«o»iled, «Gr»atitude, and acronym starts like «A»IOps. A few rare proper-name starts are also negative, e.g. «De» Pere around -9 and «L»aver around -3. There is also a diffuse weak negative, about -1 to -4, on function words and verbs in fluent, abstract or self-help prose (to, a, the, your, is, of).

L08_N8359_neg.wrong_label: Strong negatives on generic information/content mass nouns that serve as the subject or topic of a meta-statement about that material, typically in website disclaimers, privacy policies, data-handling text or reviews. Examples: "The information provided...", "All the data are provided as...", "Content posted on...", "The opinions expressed in this Newsletter", "information transmitted from your computer", "the content is what you want", "the data in the bean is", "fact checking", "Everything is super". The noun itself carries the peak (−6 to −10). The following verbs and words (is, provided, posted, collected, will be, are) get −1 to −4. Similar nouns inside the same kind of text but not as the clause subject are weaker (−1 to −4): "more information at", "files on your web site", "values", "things you need", "evidence", "suggestions".

L08_N8509_neg.wrong_label: Strong. It fires on the token 'sub' (or ' sub', ' Sub') when used as the prefix meaning subordinate, nested or a component part. Examples: sub-items, subcategory, subgoals, subdomains, sub-activities, sub-type, subwoofer, subunits, sub-agencies, subevents, sub-committee, subfields, subdivide, subframing. The activation sits on the 'sub' token itself; the following piece (-items, category, goals) stays near 0. It is strongest when 'sub' is a separate token meaning a lower level of a hierarchy, especially after enumerations or category talk ('categories, items and sub-items'). It is weaker for lexicalized words like 'Subsidy' (-3) and 'subdivide' (-3).

L08_N8509_pos.wrong_label: Short adverbial phrases that anchor a point or stage in a sequence with a deictic or ordinal noun phrase rather than describing an event. Examples: "After this, however", "At that point", "At this point", "by this time", "From now", "After a third warning,", "For Weeks 3 and 4", "Another call, and another", "Those three accounted for", "crosses a threshold". The strongest values fall on the anchor head (this, point, third, now, 3) and on the comma closing the phrase. They can also appear on a comma or clause after a recap of prior events, as in "If you start to shiver, go" or "have tied themselves in knots, you".

L08_N8930_neg.wrong_label: Tokens inside an illustrative example or quoted instance, or a near-verbatim reuse of an earlier phrase where content is being copied rather than varied. Examples: dictionary example sentences after 'definition 2:' ('- They **are** about **the** office', about −7); 'Example: to offer **someone a**' (about −6); 'Resolutions are "I want to **get** an agent"' (about −5); requirement specs ('user must be **able** to', about −5); 'For **example**, a job...' (about −4); a repeated phrase 'With notably rare exceptions**,**' (about −5); a repeated menu path 'User's menu -> settings -> **messages**' (about −4); 'It's **a** Girl' after 'It's a Boy' (about −3); 'Windows **7**' after 'Windows Vista was version 6.0' (about −3); a reformatted time 'tod at **7:**00' (about −7).

L08_N8930_pos.wrong_label: Collective or institutional group nouns that are the audience, recipient or beneficiary of something, typically after 'to/for/with' or in 'you and your X'. Examples: 'to its media customers', 'to interested community groups', 'the government... or the media', 'businesses and the public', 'agricultural community', 'you and your children', 'your diabetes team', 'shown to the authorities', 'governments in Havana', 'give developers ... their applications'. The 'of' following a group noun ('editors of', 'manufacturers of', 'community of people') is often strongly negative, as strong as −10. Coordinators and determiners inside these group phrases ('and', 'the', 'your') take weak negatives.

L08_N9703_neg.wrong_label:
Fires on the verb or preposition head that governs a following object, especially when that object is a repeated, previously mentioned or specific thing. The strongest cases are speech or report verbs about repeating content:
- "Had you asked(−10) me(−8) the(−4) same question"
- "I have asked(−6) this question"
- "I've probably said(−5) this"
- "many users have reported(−5) that", "came across(−5)"
Other examples:
- "held(−5) the top slot", "make(−5) this up"
- "modify(−4) your payment info", "Not including(−4) the required"
- "since I last taught(−4)", "made(−3) the comments", "goes about(−3) it"
- Bid boilerplate: "for/para(−4/−5) this job/este trabajo"
The pronoun or article right after the verb can also be negative ("me", "the"). Weak −1 to −3 values appear on light verbs and prepositions ("on", "to", "see", "do", "when", "last time", "the only place … where").

L08_N9703_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that bound something within a reference period, especially 'of' right after an ordinal or superlative + noun: 'first set loss OF the tournament', 'first homer OF the NLCS', 'highest score OF the day', 'first home run OF 2011'. These hit about −8 to −10, and the following 'the' gets about −3 to −4. Related temporal-limit phrasing also goes negative: 'until you obtain…' and 'don't heat up until the end', 'half way through this month', 'closed Thursday for Thanksgiving', 'September 23rd', 'usually get a second look', 'released an awesome new…' (about −5 to −8). Weaker negatives (about −1 to −3) appear on years, dates, digits and 'to' in 'decided to run'.

L12_N0056_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the interior or connector token of a fixed multi-word expression, at the point where the rest of the phrase is almost fully determined. It reads as 'we are inside a frozen collocation and the next token is forced.' The activation sits on the token just before the predictable completion, not on the completion itself. Strongest cases: "each and| every", "a.k|.a.", "call-to|-action" / "calls to| action", "sought| after", "second to| none", "trial and| error", "free of| charge", "Washington,| D.C.", "pass|ers by", "End-to|-end", "[email| protected]". Weaker cases: "over and| over", "more and| more", "Electoral| College", "Puerto| Rico", "Arabian| Nights", "United States of| America", "bear in| mind", "B&|B"-style "Bar &| Hostel", "erectile| dysfunction".

L12_N0056_pos.wrong_label: Moderate activations (+2 to +5) on nouns that name a property, quantity or attribute belonging to some entity. Examples: name / names(ake) / nameless ("the song's name is", "as the name states", "victim's name has not been released"); value / valuations; price tag; numbers; current; space; data in a quota sense ("1 GB data plan", "data allowance"); answer ("the female answer to"); material support; picture of life; details. Often the following copula or verb also gets a smaller positive value (is/has/been +2 to +4), as in "space is a premium" and "name has not been released". Weak positives (+1) appear on numbers, units and scattered concrete nouns. A small positive also shows on "we have clearly explained" inside privacy text.

L12_N0306_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the content noun that names a sub-part or element inside a larger structure, especially in descriptions of layout, composition, or contents. Examples: "polygon" (map region), "section"/"sections", "icons" on a desktop, "panes: one", "box next to", "charges" on a bill, "entries" in a matrix, "boundaries" of octets, "line going up", "frequency range", "spaces", "flecks", "pieces", "forums", "categories", "rule(s)". Typical frames are "there will be a ___", "contains ___", "features boxed ___", "cut into 4 equal ___" and "two panes: one". The activation sits on the part-noun itself, or on the "one" that picks out a part. Neighboring words (prepositions, determiners, a following "that"/"going up") get small values of +1 to +3.

L12_N0306_pos.wrong_label: Fires on a token whose spelling starts with the letters c-a (in any case), in the form 'ca', 'Ca', 'CA', 'Cah', 'Cas', 'Cat', 'CAS'. It is strongest when that token is a short subword fragment inside a proper noun or rare word: Kin|ca|id, Or|ca, Ur|ca, Cir|ca, In|ca, Al|ca|zar, electro|ca|utery, Cah|ill, 'CAS' as an acronym (CAS number, CASA), Splinter|Cat, Cat used as a name, Casino in a run-together name. Related letter shapes ('kat' in Venkat, 'Cass', 'cave', 'Carr') fire moderately. Common full English words starting with ca/cap/car fire only weakly: care, camera, Camp, Cart, Catalog, cape, cancer, candidates, Canada, cocaine, carry, cocoa.

L12_N0608_neg.wrong_label: A number followed by a plural countable noun that names a set of discrete items or entities, typical of listicles, titles and enumerations. Examples: '36 Days of Type', '12 common reasons ... and', '17 heads of state', '7 Whole Grains', '81 songs,', 'Five Strategies to', 'eleven different functions', '40 Women Who', 'Four Legends', 'Seven Tools of', '16 competitors we researched,'. The strongest negative lands on the head noun or the word right after it, such as 'of', 'Who', 'to', ',' or 'and', reaching −7 to −10. 'Days' scores −10 here because it is a title-like count of items, not a duration.

L12_N0608_pos.wrong_label: Mainly the FIRST digit, or the space just before the first digit, of a number that gives a measurement, especially the converted value in a unit conversion. Typical spots: just after '(' or '/' in pairs like '120 kilometers (75 miles)', '2.65 in (67.31 mm)', '4.75" / 12cm', '118 F (48 C)', '[67.5 x', '15.7 km2'. The '(' itself gets a small bump (+1 to +4). Also fires on the space or first digit of race times and years in sports and history text ('time of 44.4', 'Seed Time: 7.77', 'in 4:32', 'since the 1500'). A second, weaker cluster is networking and server prose: words about ports, IP bindings, protocols, UDP packets, ISPs blocking VPNs, traffic shaping, host and port fields. In 'have a binding to all IP addresses and to ensure that' or 'do I need to open ports', the verb or preposition just before the key noun gets +3 to +7. Same for ':' in 'localhost:8' and 'IP and'.

L12_N1415_neg.wrong_label: Fires on performance, specification or benefit terms in promotional, technical or product-feature text, especially the head noun of a quantity being boasted about. Examples: 'impressive torque and smooth power' (torque −7, power −4), '630 hp' (−6), 'autonomy up to 300km' (km −6), 'high yields' (−5), 'residue-free' (−5), 'reducing viral load' (−5), 'increase alkalinity and pH to desired levels' (pH −5), 'never been so easy' (−6), 'highest incidence of Cystic Fibrosis' (−5/−6), 'cannot recognize' (−6). It also gives moderate negatives on list or clause terminators in spec or technical lists (newline, ',', '?' at −2 to −5) and on numbers and units.

L12_N1415_pos.wrong_label: Seeing, watching, noticing, or drawing attention toward a person or thing. It fires on the token right after a perception or attention verb, which is usually the object pronoun or determiner of the thing being looked at. It also fires on the perception verb itself and on preposition links like 'at', 'to', 'from'. Examples: 'see|6', 'watching his|7 operation', 'watching us and taking|6 stock', 'pointed his baton at|6 me', 'draws the eye to|6', 'draws attention to your|5', 'notice a|5 big group', 'aware of the many pairs of eyes that were watching|5 her|4', 'expose their|6 uniform', 'pull away from your|6 midsection', 'make your|5 face look red', 'noticeable|5 ribs', 'accentuates|6'. Overall theme: visibility, being seen, gaze or attention aimed at a target.

L12_N1735_neg.wrong_label: Expository cell and molecular biology about protein structures and aggregates. Strongest on cytoskeleton and assembly nouns: 'Microtubules and actin filaments are' (actin about −10, 'ub' −8, 'ules' −6, 'and'/'are' about −5). Also strong on 'Oligomeric' (−6), 'intraneuronal neurofibrillary' (−3 to −4), 'The de-' (−4), and 'a specific topoisomerase inhibitor' (−3). It is milder (−1 to −3) on function words in explanatory, definitional or religious sentences: 'as in what direction', 'by nature are', 'that is flanked'.

L12_N2053_pos.wrong_label:
Strong and clean. It fires on the token immediately BEFORE the adverb 'there', i.e. where the model expects 'there' to come next.
- 'out' in 'out there' (-8 to -10): 'so much content is out there', 'providers out there', 'any of you out there'. It still fires when the next word is something else, as in 'what's out on the market' (-8).
- Verbs or copulas followed by locative 'there' (-8 to -9): 'I was there', 'it is there', 'still live there', 'help us get there'.
- Commas or connectives that may introduce existential 'there' (-3 to -8): 'That said,' then 'there are…'; 'In addition,'; 'Nonetheless,'; 'After mass,'; 'Besides X,'. Also 'While' (-4) in 'While I was there'.
The 'there' token itself is NOT active.

L12_N2552_neg.wrong_label: Function words inside conventional multiword idioms and set phrases, firing where the rest of the idiom is highly predictable. Activation sits on the connective or preposition in the middle of the phrase. Examples: 'rest OF' (+6 to +8, as in 'last the rest of', 'for the rest of', 'make it fit the rest of'); 'life OF' in 'for the life of'; 'shape of MY life'; 'true TO size'; 'suit / fits / fit' in 'fit your needs', 'suit their culture'; 'vary slightly FROM what appears ON'; 'stunning IN person than ON'; 'from the beginning TO THE end'; 'as IT gets'; 'wise beyond HIS years'; 'up to AND beyond'; 'made IN', 'measured BY', 'over the course of', 'every time'.

L12_N2552_pos.wrong_label: Stronger negative (-3 to -10) inside predicates that state the speaker's or addressee's own condition, possession or ability. Typical frames are "I have a ...", "you are ...", "if you have ...", "If I still had ...", "my skills are even lower than ...", "I play on a regular PS". The activation lands on the auxiliary or verb, the article, or the degree word right after the pronoun. Examples: "you are over the age of" (are -7), "If you are not sure" (-7), "if you have any questions" (have -6, you -5), "I have a serious fond" (a -7), "I have a pretty good feeling and understanding about" (pretty -5, about -8), "I still had a night life" (had -6), "worker has nowhere to turn" (-5), "You were chubby" (-5). A few attribute or dependency phrases also go strongly negative: "variation in hair density" (hair -10, in -3), "depending on the BPM" (on -7, the -6).

L12_N3052_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the content token that refers back to and singles out one specific member of a set, pair or contrast already set up in the left context. Typical cases: "the water on their RIGHT side and left side"; "one EXTREME of the spectrum"; "ONE part used as a lid"; "One HAND is…"; "I chose the CHOCOLATE cupcake" after "chocolate and vanilla"; "OSCAR said" after "parents, Oscar and Cynthia"; "JOHN comes with" after the four Beatles are listed; "June 20th" after "June 19, 20, and 21"; "select 'AAAA'" after first and second paragraphs were defined; "motivational CONTEXT" contrasted with cognitive; "NORTHbound lanes"; "left LUNG"; "raise RIGHT leg"; "First Chakra: Root CHAKRA". It also fires on abbreviation↔expansion mappings: "BRD – Business REQUIREMENT Document"; "zettabyte (ZB)" (strongest on Z and B); "Guarulhos (GRU)"; "Bachelor of Arts (B.A.)". The peak lands on the head or key word of the chosen item or abbreviation, often the second word of a two-word item (Requirement, side, extreme, chakra). Activation spills weakly onto the next 1–2 tokens.

L12_N3077_neg.wrong_label:
Fires on the token immediately BEFORE a likely word of intention, purpose, design or volition. That next word is something like intention(s), intent, intended, desire, willingness, purpose, meant, designated (for), 'for personal use', 'up to you', 'on your mind'. The activation sits on the predicting slot, which is usually a possessive, determiner, copula, negation or modifier. Examples:
- 'announces **his** [intention]' -10
- 'with **the** [explicit intent]' -10
- 'it**'s** [up to you]' -8
- 'is **not** [intended]' -3
- 'increased **their** [willingness]' -7
- 'the one it **was** [designated for]' -6
- 'retain their **original** [public meaning]' -6
- 'all **good** [intentions]' -5
- 'have **no** [desire]' -3
- 'This pattern **is** [for personal use only]' -4
- 'what **was** [on your mind]' -4
- 'had **malicious** [code/intent]' -6
Similar anticipatory slots also fire weakly, such as tokens before a stated consequence or function ('This led to', 'fund is insurance', 'scallops also brought'). Nearby tokens in the same clause often show small negatives (-1 to -2).

L12_N3643_neg.wrong_label: Negative values come from digits inside dates and timestamps in forum post headers. Examples: '07-19-2003' (digits about -4 to -7), 'Posted 27 June 2003 - 04|-8:26 PM', and 'Apr 26, 2011'. Also negative are tokens in stock boilerplate that come just before the key word. Examples: 'up|-10-to-date web browser', 'Work Step by|-8 Step', 'Ad blocker interference detected|-5', 'for viewers|-5', 'further modifications|-6', 'custom ad blocker rule|-6', 'Version 3.8.7' (-2 to -3), and HTML tag lists ('<i|-6>'). Text ending 'ISO8859|-6' also goes negative.

L12_N3643_pos.wrong_label:
Content nouns or names, plus some verbs, that repeat an entity already mentioned or fill a parallel slot in a list. These are often a subject or head noun just before or as the verb of a report or comparison. The negative usually lands on the head noun or verb right after the repeated name or parallel modifier, with smaller negatives on the following 1-2 tokens. Examples:
- "Kai's Cats" after Kai was already introduced
- "South Africa's" in a country list
- "Bangladeshi households" after "Black Caribbean households"
- "Sheriff's deputies say"
- "the researchers noted"
- "other galleries"
- "warm drinks" in a list of fluids
- "animals and plants survive"
- "Dearborn received" in a list of award winners
- "poke around"
- "when we provide"
- "the author Louis"

L12_N3852_neg.wrong_label: Narration of what happens next in a sequence of steps or a scheduled event: directions and instructions ('At the first turn off, take…', 'Go down 14 tiles and hang…', 'select one tile and after that…', 'Continue on far enough and you will…'). Also announcements of when or where an event happens ('The first will take place on Saturday', 'The concert will be held on May 9', 'Wednesday, Dec. 18, at 6:30pm, we're adding…', 'This pair will disappear and you will earn…', 'stayed overnight in', 'coming up in two weeks', 'see you again at next year's'). The activation sits on the predicate or connective that moves the timeline forward: 'will', 'take place', 'held', 'turn', 'and', 'with', 'again', 'overnight', 'weeks', and the time token 'pm' or the comma after a date or time in a schedule.

L12_N3852_pos.wrong_label: Dominant pole. The token 'When'/'when' introducing a temporal or conditional clause in procedural, instructional, technical or industrial text (manuals, product descriptions, safety warnings, how-to steps, event listings). Strongest when 'when' introduces a reduced clause: a gerund or participle, or an adjective with no subject. Examples: 'When purchasing the production line' -10, 'when filling large doses' -9, 'when ready click' -7, 'When installing' -6, 'when personnel enter or exit the clean room' -6, 'when viewed as' -5, 'When coupled with' -5, 'when using the trampoline' -5, 'When used in' -4. Also an event-listing label 'When: Sept.' -5. Instructional 'When you/we + verb' (operating a product or procedure) gives -3 to -6. Small -1 can appear on 'size', 'one', 'during', 'whole', 'largest', 'of'.

L12_N4096_neg.wrong_label: Pieces of less-common common nouns or foreign words broken into fragments, usually the first or a middle piece, outside a person-name slot: «Fer»ries, «pul»lover, «Pel»ican, «mor»atorium, «ang»ler, Pr«un»us, «mer»idia, Ry«uk»yu «arch»ipel»ago, «Fuk»ui, m«er»ck. Mojibake and stray byte tokens are also strongly negative: '�' (e.g. after '4,200'), 'â', '€', and a garbled Greek letter. Milder negatives (around −3) occur on tokens like 'best' in 'bestseller' or 'best friends', 'American', and 'Lak'ewood.

L12_N4472_neg.wrong_label: Neutral or analytic statements about quantities, proportions and comparisons, especially in reports, statistics, specs or prices. Strongest examples: "many" / "them" in "many of them could not" (−10, −7); "is" in "the oldest is married" (−9); the digits of "720p" (−8); the digits and % in "than 30%" (−7). Other cases: "can get three products for under", "less than the cost of a latte", "the views of CEOs", "officials… have likely never heard", "consumers are most responsive to", "when there is 70% light output", "Rules 2002". Fires on the quantifier, comparative ("than", "under", "less"), "of", the copula/auxiliary, or the digits.

L12_N4472_pos.wrong_label: Strongest on (1) smiley or laughing emojis (🙂, 😀) placed at the end of a sentence or post as a friendly sign-off, and (2) plural common nouns naming groups of people or things, often sentence-initial or the object of address. Examples: Functions/functions, bloggers, programmers, applicants, wrinkles, Witnesses. Weaker negatives (−1 to −3) fall on generic abstract or common nouns and adjectives (quality, materials, casual, support, conductors, collaborative) and on some place names in an SEO or listing context (Dhabi, Nebraska).

L12_N4872_neg.wrong_label: Fires on tokens of a technical or domain term, usually a compound noun, that the passage is introducing, defining or explaining. The strongest values fall on the core subword of the term's head, especially when it is being defined. Examples: 'What is absorption costing? / Absorption costing goes by…' gives -7 on 'absorption' and -10 on 'orption', with -1 to -4 on 'costing'. Others: 'Hal|ogen' bulbs (-3), hip 'dys|pl|asia' (-2 to -3 on 'pl'), 'pass through entities' (-3/-2), 'S Corporations' (-2), 'Diastolic pressure' (-2), 'fixed rate' (-2), 'amino acids' (-2), 'array index' (-2). Weaker cases include an ellipsis mid-explanation ('you can…use them', -3), a label colon ('UPC Code:', -3) and 'Reviewed by' (-2). Magnitude grows when the term is being defined (questions like 'What is X?' or 'X is…'), when it is repeated, and when it is rare or jargon-like.

L12_N5391_pos.wrong_label: The final subword/token that completes a specific named entity or kind-name, especially a taxonomic, genre, or product term: Metal|lica, sorgh|um, Ch|eddar, magn|olia, melanog|aster, marcesc|ens, apple (trees), Deep House, afro-be|at, pe|ony, pine, latex, cherry (gelato), Bieber, heavy rock, indoor (air), the closing quote after a song title (“7 Rings”). Possessives and quantifier/ordinal builds inside descriptive noun phrases also fire weakly to moderately: Norwegian’s international, Schroder's ... their share, first-ever. Typical magnitude is +3 to +6. Weaker spread of +1 to +2 falls on nearby determiners and modifiers (its, the, new, of).

L12_N5447_neg.wrong_label: Moderate positive (+2 to +5) on a noun or name token that completes a conventional, highly predictable phrase. Examples: disclaimer lists ('completeness', 'accuracy', 'reliability', 'suitability', 'usefulness' in 'no warranties... about the accuracy...'); news source credits ('(AP)', 'LiveScience', 'M.D.'); site and credit boilerplate ('Original Design by', 'Creative Commons', 'Edit', 'updates' in Terms of Service); kitchen-appliance nouns in recipes ('blender', 'food processor'); a word closing a set phrase ('wisdom', 'enigma', 'Hoax', 'anti-inflammatory', 'broken English', 'OpenTable', 'Politician', 'In the Clinic'). These are weaker and more diffuse than the negative pole.

L12_N5447_pos.wrong_label: Mid-number digit tokens, mostly '2' (sometimes '4' or '3'), that come after a multi-digit prefix not ending in 7. Examples: ZIP 97«2»02, 53«2»12, 7«2»035, 47«4»48; Form 53«2»9; price 0.67«2»0. Peaks are moderate, about +2 to +4. Very weak (+1 to +2) on a name fragment right after a short capitalised syllable like Sad/Nad (Sad«hb»ela, Sad«iv», Nad«ine»), and on odd tokens like ' Pediatric'. Also about +1 on a hyphen inside a phone number (800-853«-»1403).

L12_N5932_neg.wrong_label:
The dominant, strong pole (down to -10). It fires on the first token immediately after a stranded verb or verb+preposition whose object has been extracted. This happens in relative clauses or wh-constructions where the object comes earlier ('what X will look like', 'cities for retirees to relocate to', 'the problems you may be experiencing'). The token right after the gap carries the activation. That token is typically:
- a preposition: with, in, by, for, after, to, from, about, on
- punctuation: '.' or ','
- a stray verb: is, doing
It signals that the parser expects the object slot to be empty and the clause to end or continue.
Examples:
- 'relocate to «with»' ≈ -10
- 'look like «in» two decades' ≈ -10
- 'will look like«.»' ≈ -9
- 'experiencing «by»' ≈ -9
- 'buy from today on«.»' ≈ -9
- 'had «after»' ≈ -7
- 'known for «is»' ≈ -7
- 'is performing«,»' ≈ -7
- 'pose «to» societies' ≈ -7
- 'make «about»' ≈ -7
- 'get «for» your home' ≈ -6
Smaller follow-on negatives of -1 to -5 can occur on later tokens of the same continuation ('based on', 'your').

L12_N5932_pos.wrong_label: The head noun, or the noun-like token, that closes a noun phrase naming a category, type, domain or specific entity, usually right after modifiers or a compound prefix. Examples: 'last-**gen** ... **systems**' (−10), 'any science-**related** **topic**' (−7/−5), 'Fitness **Centers**' (−7), 'residential **docks**' (−7), 'their own domain **name**' (−6), '**Houston**'s new flights' (−6), 'the rest **of** the league', 'Citation **Format**', 'X. laevis' (−6), '3100 **block** of', 'Kindle **ebooks**', 'pedal cleats', 'severe **weather**'. Determiners right before such a head ('all of **the** freshmen') can also go negative.

L12_N6170_pos.wrong_label: Text about quantities of a vital or game resource being generated, restored, increased or depleted. Clearest in gaming mechanics: threat generation, health bars, healing, HPS, damage pulses, perks for health, 'increases her ... range', diminishing returns. It generalizes to real-world vitality and survival: 'restoring life', 'life threatening', 'lifesaving', 'oxygen-depleted', 'nutrient-deficient', 'battery can run down', 'plumb tuckered out', adrenal fatigue, 'save valuable ammunition'. Scuba and diving contexts also fire (PADI, 'Diving With Air & Nitrox', dive duration numbers), as do health-profession labels. Activation sits on the word that names or quantifies the resource ('life', 'health', 'oxygen', 'nutrient', 'extra') or the verb or preposition just before the quantity ('generate', 'of', 'on', 'run', 'heal', '2').

L12_N6717_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token that names the whole set in a partitive or ordinal-of-total construction: 'two of three', 'third of five', 'six of the seven', '31 of 32', '3 of 5', 'first of several/many', 'one of six/several', 'youngest of 11'. The activation sits on the total/quantifier word right after 'of' (or 'of the'), and sometimes weakly on 'of' itself or the noun that follows. The top activation (+10) is an outlier: '=' after a key in a key=value template ('subdivision =', 'date =', +5). Weak firing also appears on field-separator colons in label:value lists ('Exhibit EEEE:', 'Value for money:') and on hedging or quantifier tokens ('most?', 'almost all', 'may be').

L12_N7232_pos.wrong_label: Strong activation at the boundary where one item ends and the next begins in reference lists, bibliographies, and footnote or citation lists. Examples are the next item number right after a URL or citation ('.\n4Aluminum price' gives -10 on '4'), the dash or digits that start a new reference entry ('-', ' ', '2','0' gives -3 to -5), and citation abbreviations like 'cf' and its period inside parenthetical citations ('(Mill 2004, p. 292; cf.' gives -10 on 'cf', -4 to -5 on ';' and '.'). The same holds more weakly for numbered list markers ('7', '8.') and for the '.' starting a new item after a phone number or URL (-2 to -3).

L12_N7355_neg.wrong_label: '#' used as a hashtag that directly precedes a word or name: '2015 #FNCKINGDOM' (-6), 'Kid #1' (-4), 'MLS# 157' (-3), 'daddy #tiny #loven' (-2), '#ReadyToIgnite' (-2). Also weaker negatives (-1 to -2) on title or holding words: ' Sir' (Sir Digby Jones, 'Sir, here's'), ' Holding' (Qatar Holding), ' hold' down, ' holding' fee, ' backup' dancers. Occasional -1 on tokens like 'care' and 'U.S'.

L12_N7455_neg.wrong_label: Mid-word subword pieces of unusual proper names, usually surnames or brand names: Gr|aven|ey −6, Ish|ik|awa −4, Assouline-L|ichten −4, Ele|k|tra −4, Graf|en|au −3, Drum|mond −3, Adv|an|Tex −3. Also predictable tokens inside stock or corporate phrases: "Images are kindly provided" −6 on "provided", "Most Beautiful" −5, "Canadian Review of" −5 on "of", "University of Würzburg, and the" −5 on "and", "after-sales" −4, "research and development" −4, "The Amazing Race" −4, a URL "?" −4.

L12_N7493_neg.wrong_label: Negative values also fall inside names, titles, and rare terms. The strongest is the title word 'Secretary' in 'Treasury Secretary William McAdoo' (-10). Other examples: rare technical nouns (sty(lobate), tal(us), sw(amps)), mid-syllables of foreign place names (Ş-eb-inkarah), brand or site suffixes (LibraryThing, PRWEB, ASSA ABLOY), title or role words (Dame, Fort King, Domestic), mid-surname pieces (Fab-ry), the 'at' in 'Picnic at Hanging Rock', 'Data' in 'Social Science Data Archive', and nuts-and-b(olts). Some cases are near-duplicates of positive ones, so the sign is hard to predict.

L12_N7493_pos.wrong_label: The negative pole is strong. It fires on the token of technical or classificatory adjectives and compound modifiers, usually Latin or Greek prefix compounds, that sit in front of a noun as a category label. The biggest cases are 'nonlinear' (-8 to -10), 'infrared'/'In-frared' (-6 to -10), 'multiplayer' (-6 to -7), 'extracellular' (-7) and 'aerobic' (-6). Moderate cases (-2 to -4) include 'intravenous', 'acoustic', 'freelance', 'offline', 'transgender', 'parametric', 'online', 'adrenal', 'multidisciplinary' (tokens 'multid' and 'iplinary') and 'prenatal'. Mild cases (-1) include 'electronic', 'mainstream', 'recursive', 'adaptive', 'high-resolution', 'bluetooth', 'cardio' and 'sidewalls'.

L12_N8014_pos.wrong_label: The word 'as' when it introduces a role, function, or capacity: 'use X AS a', 'with the RedHead AS my partner', 'using lottery funding AS a crutch', 'as bait', 'as inspired by', 'as well', 'as a general rule', 'gone AS soon as', 'track my steps AS I strive'. These 'as' tokens hit -7 to -10. The token right after 'as' is also negative: 'a' or 'my' around -4 to -7. Verbs that set up 'as' carry weaker negatives: 'use' and 'them' around -3 to -5. Possessives in a role sense are also mildly negative, e.g. 'Logic was MY crutch' at -7 and 'She's my own' at -4.

L12_N8067_pos.wrong_label: Fires in step-by-step instructional or procedural text, mainly on the sentence-ending period, newline, or comma right after an instruction or step is completed, where the next sentence is likely to start with 'Now', 'Then', 'Once', 'First', 'Repeat' or 'Again'. Examples: 'Test movement.' -> Now; 'register.' -> The process…; 'get here.' -> Now right click; 'see instructions below).' -> Once. The strongest negative value (-10) is on 'but' in narrative setup sequencing: 'took forever to set it up but [once we got]'. It also fires on nouns near scheduling or process language ('estimate on the duration of the import process [tomorrow]').

L12_N8458_pos.wrong_label: The first fragment of a word the tokenizer splits into pieces, usually an 'f'/'F' piece. L16_N8165_neg.wrong_label: Physically placing, covering, resting, or moving a body part or worn accessory. It peaks on the preposition or possessive after a placement or covering verb, and on accessory nouns. Examples: 'hid my teary face under|-10 my|-8 hair', 'lowered|-6 her|-4 head|-4', 'placed|-6 her hands on|-4 his', 'flopped|-6 back on|-3 the couch', 'perfect for|-5 resting|-6 your|-6 feet', 'doffs|-5 his|-5 hat', 'glasses flung|-5', 'wrap|-5 back up'. Words for sunglasses and eyewear such as 'Sunglasses|-7', 'aviator sunglasses|-5' and 'sunglass|-4' are strongly negative. Clothing and accessory nouns like sweater, gloves and wristwatch give weak negatives of −1 to −3.

L16_N8165_pos.wrong_label: Strong. It fires on the phrase 'when it comes to' that follows an evaluative claim about someone or something ('X is the best / an ace / hopeless / experienced ... when it comes to Y'). 'when' and 'it' carry most of the activation, roughly -5 to -10 each. 'comes' gets about -1 to -2, and 'to' gets almost nothing. The same pattern applies to variants such as 'when it pertains to', 'when it is a question of', and 'when considering' after a comparison. Preceding evaluative words ('hopeless', 'trust', 'offer', 'king', 'character', 'experienced') can reach about -1 to -2. The 'as' of 'as far as' gets about -1 to -2.

L16_N8712_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the first token (often a subword fragment) of a proper name, especially a place or street name in an address or location list, where the model must predict how the name continues. Typical cases: 'Cal' in Calle / Calabasas / Calhoun / Calvary (+6 to +8); 'W' and especially '.' in street addresses like '100 W. Imperial Highway' or '1501 W. Badger Rd.' (+4 to +7); 'Stone' in 'of Stone[ Mountain]', 'Saint' in 'Saint John', 'west' in 'west LA' (+4 to +5); 'BUCHAREST' (+5). It also fires on opening fragments of foreign surnames and titles ('Mur' and 'avs' in Muravschi, 'Cap' in Capriccio, 'Mal'/'ac' in Malacca, 'z' in Amzulescu) and on the '(' that opens a parenthetical name or country code ('(Lohengrin)', '(BA)') at +1 to +3. There are rarer weak hits inside formulaic multi-token phrases ('of' in 'flask of ointment of pure', 'correct' in 'how to correct material', 'or' in a medical list), and occasional digits in dates or DOIs.

L16_N8712_pos.wrong_label: Tokens inside templated web boilerplate and inside brand or product names, especially in lists. Examples: e-commerce platform lists (Op|enc|art, Os|commerce, 3|dc|art, OpenCart™ is a trademark of Open|Cart); forum footers ('Powered by vBulletin', with the peak on ' by'); forum post timestamps (' PM' after a time like 02:38); copyright year ranges (2000 - 2016); freelancer-marketplace spam ('5 freelancers están/estão ofertando'); stock privacy and contact lines ('functionality of our website', 'get back to you', 'accessible to any and all users'); file sizes ('31KB'); counts such as '404 Facebook Shares'. Also fires on mid-word subword pieces of uncommon proper names (Sum|it|omo, Emmy|l|ou, Str|atos, St|rel|ka, mambo-develop|er).

L16_N8941_neg.wrong_label: Digits and separators inside post or email metadata: timestamps (the seconds digits after the minutes colon, e.g. '14:29:08', where ':' gets ~+4 and the next digit up to +9), dates in headers ('Date: 2003-...'), and view counts or post IDs ('Viewed 179', '617 Views', '#11069', '4 years ago'). Also boilerplate tokens in news datelines ('Newswise'). The context is forum or mailing-list header and footer metadata.

L16_N8941_pos.wrong_label:
Function words after a noun or verb that open a complement whose object refers back to something already established. The object is usually an anaphor or definite back-reference: "it", "that", "them", "the state", "the field", "the disorder". Strongest on the preposition or verb itself:
- "if you have knowledge with that": "have" / "knowledge" / "with" = -10
- "turned to Pozament": "to" = -10
- "a single from it", "every song from it": "from" = -9
- "institute of study in the field": "in" = -9
- "performers at": "at" = -8
- "people without the disorder": "without" = -8
- "but after that": "after" = -7
- "business in the state": "business" / "in" = -7
- "season for my hobby": "for" = -7
- "and rate them": "rate" = -7
Weaker cases: "club in world football", "relating to", "associated with", "five of them".

L20_N0748_neg.wrong_label:
The dominant, clear behavior. It fires on a subword token containing 'ar' that sits inside a longer word, usually a proper name or a rare word split into pieces. The strongest trigger is 'amar' (-8 to -10), as in Cat|amar|ca, cat|amar|an, D|amar, J|amar, T|amar, K|amar|u and aqu|amar|ine. Close variants are similarly strong (about -8 to -9): 'dar' (Mas|dar), 'gar' (Al|gar|ve) and 'iar' (Plag|iar|ism). Weaker variants:
- 'ar' inside complement|ar|ities: about -5.
- Word-initial name pieces like 'Mar' (Mar|thur, the month 'Mar'): about -4 to -5.
- 'har' and 'ear' (st|ear|ate): about -3 to -4.
- 'Gar' and 'Ar' at the start of a split name: about -3.
- 'Kumar', 'VER', 'CHAR': about -1 to -3.

L20_N0748_pos.wrong_label: Strong. Fires on digits that open a field in structured, formatted metadata rather than prose. Strongest on the leading '0' of zero-padded dates and times in forum or post timestamps: '|01-13' (−10), '07-19-2003, |07:07' (−7), 'View Single Post↵|07-06' (−9), '|02-21-2009, |01:24' (−7/−8). Also strong on separators or tokens just before a number in citation, profile or spec fields: 'vol. 33|(1)' (−8), 'member for 2 years|, 2 months' (−8), 'Date posted: |August 2' (−8), 'fe80|::' (−7), file sizes '26|.6 MB' and '13|.57' (−5 to −7), zero digits inside ZIP-code lists (−5 to −7). Weaker (−1 to −4) on date, time, rank and verse fields in semi-structured text: 'born April| 23', '#5', 'Peter 3|:15', 'Sunday, |6:30', 'Posted by X |5/15/2007 |9:05'.

L20_N0854_neg.wrong_label: Hypothetical, conditional or unknown situations, where the speaker reasons about something not given or poses a what-if or diagnostic question. Examples: "How about 27" (about, −8), "if you turn this to just air, does the fan..." (does, −7), "where it mounts" (where, −6), "without seeing what" (what, −6), "you might be having" (having, −5), "if he simply uses" (uses, −5), "You didn't say what type of medication she is on" (on, −5), "If it is built in" (is, −5; in, −4), "If I have kids," (comma, −4), "he might look like" (like, −4), "describe it as" (as, −4). The activation falls on the verb, wh-word or preposition right after the conditional, modal or question frame.

L20_N0862_neg.wrong_label: Programming and data-structure contexts, specifically abstract container or data nouns and the words that introduce them: 'an object', 'a dictionary containing', 'list/dictionary', 'array of', 'one-dimensional array', 'text file', 'instance variables', 'list of', 'string', 'aggregated into an overall score'. The strongest values fall on the determiner or noun right before the content is specified ('an' −10, 'containing' −9, 'object' −9, 'dictionary' −9). In code-documentation prose, function words such as 'the', 'to', 'in', and 'of' run about −1 to −5. Mild −1 values appear on recipe instruction verbs ('add', 'stir', 'and') and on generic nouns like 'slice', 'letters', 'trilogy', 'novel'.

L20_N0862_pos.wrong_label:
Rare large spikes, with no single clean theme. The biggest (+10) fell on a sentence-final '.
' that closes an explanatory paragraph and comes right before a new section heading ('...flea problem that is already there.
' followed by 'Limit Outdoor Exposure'). Other strong spikes (+4 to +8) land on a word inside a fixed multiword unit whose continuation is highly predictable. Examples: 'number' in 'features a number of', 'example' in 'significant example of', 'of' in 'warmth of the', 'site' in 'third party site', 'Advantage' in 'Medicare Advantage Plan', 'tag' in 'franchise tag', 'Out' in 'Tapped Out', 'ewire' in 'Primewire', 'firmly' in 'anchored firmly to', 'could'/'might' in hedged 'which could affect' / 'this might lead'. Weak +1 to +3 values are common on ordinary connectives in flowing prose: 'and', 'of', 'to', 'can', 'will', commas, '.', '
'. They are slightly more frequent in promotional, advice or bio-style text.

L20_N1288_neg.wrong_label: The preposition "of" or "de" inside formal institution or proper-name titles: Gallery of Art, Academy of Visual Arts, Royal College of Anaesthetists, Court of Appeal, House of Lords, Museum of Natural History, Hôtel de Ville, Gîte de France. These run -3 to -5, peaking on "of"/"de", with neighbouring name words (Gallery, Royal, Visual, Natural) at -1 to -3. Real-estate room descriptions are weaker, around -1 to -3 ("formal dining room", "separate bathroom", "the living room"). "for" in product titles gives about -1.

L20_N1288_pos.wrong_label: Induction-like copying. It fires on tokens that repeat a word or phrase already seen earlier in the window, so the model can predict them by copying. The peak is usually on the last or a later token of the repeated span, and nearby tokens are often mildly positive. Examples: the second "children 2 and under" (+6–7 on 'and under'); "side cut out" (+7 on 'out'); "Manly" after "Manly Beach" earlier (+6 on 'ly'); "Peter Blowes" (+6 on 'es'); "Near Mint" (+6); "tiara", "guild", "guitar duet", "Katy Perry", "Wayback Machine", "Iran", "Rodenstock", "Dee Dee", "Screenlife", "Patrick Ford", and "16in and 24" (all +6). It also fires on recurring dates and number patterns, e.g. "12th" after "14th" (+6). It is strongest for ordinary English words, names, or phrases recurring within list-like or descriptive text.

L20_N1449_neg.wrong_label: Strongest on tokens inside machine-spun, word-salad, or keyword-stuffed web spam. This includes pharma spam, essay-mill spam, SEO gibberish, and scrambled 'Culture War... civil l' style text, where syntax is broken and the next word is unpredictable. The activation lands on function words, conjunctions, prepositions, punctuation, and odd content words mid-garble ('civil l' -10, 'dedication to' -8, 'her other' -7, 'applicants' -7, 'will' -6, 'and' -5, 'searching' -5, 'in' -5). A second trigger is truncation and boundary artifacts in scraped snippets: a newline right after a word cut off mid-word ('su↵', 'bus↵', 'located in↵' -5 to -6), ellipses '...' or '....' ending a truncated excerpt (-3 to -5), and stray periods or commas in list-like fragments (-3 to -6). Activation grows the deeper the text sits in incoherence, often building over several consecutive tokens (-1, -2, -3 ... then a spike).

L20_N1449_pos.wrong_label: Tokens deep inside opaque, non-word character strings such as URL shortener IDs (pic.twitter.com/1yWMWWGT3q, amzn.to/2GSkbNv, ift.tt/1G7Kd7X, goo.gl/eh0Ua), YouTube video IDs, hex colors (#ecea26), IPv6 addresses, dimension strings (1280x1024, 300x75), codes (T48.3X5S, 280E), and version or part numbers. The activation lands on a single digit or letter chunk several characters into the string, usually near its end, after the model has seen enough of it to know it is gibberish or alphanumeric. Digits within numeric runs (the 0 in 1280x, 240v) are typical carriers.

L20_N2066_neg.wrong_label: Mostly in Catholic or devotional text. It fires on descriptive, quantifying or evaluative words about saints, virtues, sacraments or religious life. The strongest case is a number that counts a sacred enumeration: 'the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit' (seven −10, then of/the −4). Other examples: 'seven demons' −3; 'Veronica was a pious woman' (pious −5); 'The Blessed' −4; 'lived a perfect life without sin' (without −4); 'live your commitment' (your −4); 'the saint's other accomplishments' (−3); '244 Catholic colleges' (−3). Weaker cases appear outside religion: list or comparison words such as 'alongside' in a crypto article (−4), and bullet dashes in a probiotic ingredient list (−2 to −3).

L20_N2066_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that set up a report of an error or message, typical of tech-support and forum text. Examples: 'get/getting an error', 'ends in a timeout', 'throws me a', 'fails with the message', 'result in an', 'Mysql::Error:', 'contains the following messages:', '会遇到', 'NOTE:'. The strongest values (−6 to −9) fall on the verb and the article or preposition just before the error noun ('get', 'an', 'in', 'a', 'with'). Opening quotes, colons, and newlines right before the quoted error text also reach −5 to −9. The error noun itself gets about −5, and words like 'says', 'message', and 'warning' get −3 to −5. Sentence-final periods or newlines at the end of notices and warnings (shopping-cart notices, RubyGems notes) can reach −5 to −8.

L20_N2561_pos.wrong_label: The first piece of a word that the tokenizer has split, where the word is clearly unfinished and the next token completes it. Only the fragment token itself fires. It is strongest (+7 to +10) for short onset fragments, especially 'Sp'/'sp' (Sp|okesman, Sp|andex, Sp|ots, Sp|oken, sp|areribs), 'R'/'r' (R|CT, r|ashes, r|uckus, R|abbi, R|icciardo, '/R'|SD) and 'sub'. Similar strength for onsets of rare names and loanwords: Sch|wenksville, L|huillier, Pel|angi, bur|rito, K'|Hor. Occasionally a whole word fires when it sits in an odd slot, such as 'The' at the start of a title ('The| Ides of March') or a sentence-initial 'By'. Mid values (+2 to +4) come from fragments like tor|rid, revol|ting, Be|iber, BE|ER, Am|miel, sp|idery and Display inside a URL.

L20_N2667_neg.wrong_label: Sharp single-token spikes on discourse-continuation subjects deep inside conversational, narrative or news prose. These are mostly the pronouns 'we' and 'you', plus sentence- or clause-initial 'the'/'This' that follows an earlier sentence. Examples: 'would| you|-10'; 'In the year ahead, we|-9 plan'; 'ensuring the|-9 big picture'; 'reason to be concerned that the|-9 next president'; '. This|-9 work was undertaken'; 'And we|-8 are making'; 'that we|-8 were'; 'I|-5 will make'. Odd mid-token spikes also occur, such as 'high‐|-10alkali' and 'Jan.|-8'. Mild negatives of −1 to −3 appear on digits in dates, zip codes and phone numbers, on citation/metadata tokens, on proper names in datelines, and on newlines in boilerplate.

L20_N2867_neg.wrong_label: The last content word of a phrase naming the purpose, application or target activity that a method, device, drug or training is for. These are typically task or activity nouns in frames like 'used for / help with / prevention of / treatment of / to boost ___' or in noun compounds naming a function. Examples: 'low bitrate audio CODING' (+10), 'help you with your SHOOTING' (+9), 'prevention of MIGRAINE' (+9), 'chronic headache PAIN' (+8), 'level MEASUREMENT' (+6), 'biofuel PRODUCTION' (+6), 'Typhoon WARNING Center' (+6), 'fighting systems' (+6), 'functional TESTING' (+6), 'to EVALUATE' (+7), 'rail GUNS' (+7), 'face BLINDNESS' (+7), 'forecast' (+6), 'query PERFORMANCE' (+4). Ailments count when they are the condition a therapy targets (migraine, headache, face blindness).

L20_N3475_neg.wrong_label: The position in film, TV or comic writing where the next token will be an actor's or real person's name attached to a character. The strongest case is the opening parenthesis right after a character name, e.g. 'Miles (Ashton Sanders' gives about −10, 'Philip Cass (John Ericson' and 'Steve Rogers (Chris Evans' about −7 to −8. The same applies to 'played by' (−5 on 'played', −7/−8 on 'by'), 'leading' in 'leading man/roles' (−4 to −6), and a director's name followed by '(' with credits (−6). The closing ')' after the actor's name is about −2 to −3. Weaker negatives (about −3 to −5) show up on some descriptive or aesthetic words in reviews: 'patterning', 'pastel', 'campy', 'likeable', 'period' music, 'bloke'.

L20_N3475_pos.wrong_label: Strongest on e-commerce and listing result-count headers such as 'Showing 1–12 of 20', 'Displaying 1 - 10', 'Displaying reviews 1-5', 'Showing the single result'. The activation is spread across the phrase. Peaks fall on the space and '1' after Showing/Displaying (+7 to +10) and on the dash (+7 to +10). 'Showing' itself is about +5 to +8 (when it is split, the 'ing' of 'Display|ing' takes it, +6 to +8). 'of' and the trailing number or newline get +3 to +5. A weaker, related family is presentative or progressive 'arriving / showing up' phrasing: 'X is coming (soon/along/to)' +4 to +5, 'This is looking northwest', 'It's lookin' good', 'looking forward/at' +2 to +6, 'Here comes', 'Here she is', 'here we are', 'There goes the', 'approaching quickly', 'coming up' (+2 to +5).

L20_N4742_neg.wrong_label: Fires where the text is about to give, or has just begun giving, an alternative form of a term it just named. This covers translations (Hoshi no Kirby (星のカービィ; Lola la Chata ("Snub-Nose"); Tres Grandes; Nuestra Salud), pronunciations (pronounced "pickpocket"; [laːɣə]), variant spellings or minimal pairs (loathe vs. loath; Program & Programme; Gamoe (or Garmo)), parallel glosses (Basque = oliba, Finnish = olivi; yard (garden); carpe diem – seize the day) and acronym or parenthetical renamings (Pension fund (KWAP)). The peak usually sits on the separator that introduces the alternative: 'vs.', '(', '=', '&', 'or', 'pronounced', or an opening quote. It can also sit on the first one to three tokens of the alternative itself, especially foreign-script characters (Japanese, Devanagari, Korean, Chinese) or a translated phrase (the cursed souls).

L20_N4742_pos.wrong_label: Other tokens in the same kind of boilerplate, especially the following. 1) Modal or negated auxiliaries in disclaimer and aphorism sentences: " may" in "any use which may be made" (-10), " must" (-9), " cannot" (-6). 2) Head nouns or verbs that close a clause and set up the next predicate: " site" in "Wikia is a free-to-use site that" (-7 to -9), " contact" in "...information, contact" (-9), " update" in "Cannot delete or update a parent row" (-8). 3) Subject+verb starts: " have" in "We have a modified experience" (-6 to -7), " from"/" advertising" (-3 to -4), " you" (-3 to -7), and a comma before "we provide" (-9). Milder negatives of -1 to -5 show up on licensing, cookie, signup and company-blurb text.

L20_N4767_pos.wrong_label: Narratives of change over time toward improvement, availability or modernity. Typical frames: 'X is now far easier', 'more effective medications', 'lower turbine prices', 'reduction in costs', 'availability of fMRI data', 'treatments we have available are much more effective', 'now responsive', 'before they were even cool', 'yet to be seen', 'one day we'll actually have viable…'. The peak lands on the comparative or progress word ('easier', 'more', 'prices', 'costs', 'available', 'current', 'new', 'now') right after a temporal or comparative cue ('now far', 'are developing', 'lower', 'in recent years the').

L20_N4855_neg.wrong_label: The word 'joint'/'Joint' meaning shared or combined, especially when it opens an institutional name or a compound: 'Joint Commission', 'Joint Base', 'Joint Typhoon Warning Center', 'JEDEC (Joint Electronic...)', 'joint venture', 'joint declaration', 'Jointly'. The activation sits on the 'joint' token itself. Following tokens get a small spillover ('Electronic' +7, 'ly' +7, 'Typhoon' +2, 'Base' +3). The same concept spreads weakly to other togetherness words: 'jointly', 'joined together', 'join' (song credit), 'Join us/Join Forces', 'co-led', 'Co-authors', and faintly to 'United', 'unified', 'teaming', 'joins'.

L20_N4855_pos.wrong_label: Function words and continuations inside highly formulaic phrases in religious prose and step-by-step technical instructions. The strongest hits are prepositions and articles after a fixed head. Examples: 'take away the sins of' (take −7, of −7); 'Chechen Islamic Cultural' (Islamic −7); 'the goodness of the Lord' (goodness −5); 'Africa Cup of' (of −4). Instruction examples: '.htaccess file, located in the directory' (in −4); 'Deny from' (from −5); 'Order threads in' (in −5); 'File Manager' in cPanel instructions (−4); 'in the search box' (the −4). Also the newline right after 'View Single Post' (−6) or after a forum username (−4), and code fragments like '->select()->' (−4).

L20_N4916_neg.wrong_label: Deflationary or reframing statements that recast something as the same familiar thing differing only in one respect: 'just a really long one', 'little kids in bigger bodies', 'just have to get used to a new way of dialing', 'merely new expressions of', 'in another way', 'looking in different directions', 'I just never knew it', 'just a really expensive door stop', 'works the same, but instead of...'. Activation sits on the tokens that state the difference (new, different, another, bigger, really, way, instead, with, slightly differing) and on the hedges that set up the frame (just, merely, albeit). It is strongest on the head of the difference phrase, e.g. 'way' in 'new way', 'bigger' in 'in bigger bodies', 'really' in 'just a really long one'.

L20_N5110_neg.wrong_label: Subword pieces of non-English words, especially Turkish, Polish, Welsh, Danish, Norwegian and transliterated Slavic text. Examples: aydınlat«ma» −10; Naj«le»«ps»«zy» −5 to −9; Nant«-y» −6; Personalhistor«isk» −5; Zazn«acz»«ono» −5; uyar«ınca» −4. Weaker negatives (−2 to −5) fall on parts of descriptive or technical compound noun phrases: white-«l»ipped peccary, «jumping» jack, «live» AIS ship tracking, «cast» wheels, Inmarsat«-»4, the digits of dates such as 2016 in a leap-second notice, and (O)eWF acronym pieces.

L20_N5110_pos.wrong_label: Diffuse and only weakly coherent; typically +2 to +5, rarely up to +10. Two recurring groups. (1) Words in goal/motion or transfer phrases just before a destination or complement: 'help us' (+5 on 'us'), 'Get' in 'Way to Get Pitchers', 'Before I get emails', 'get your supplies where', 'transferring files between', 'Lead You To', 'move us in', 'be fully recovered', 'Twitter right HERE'. (2) Early pieces of capitalized names or brands: GE Monogram, GEAB, Stax, Oswalt, Hussey, US-ACAN, Gulf Marine, Eve's, Urban Outfitters, Mall Artha, 'Tie a Yellow Ribbon', and 'detailed information' (+7). Weak +1 to +2 also appears on ordinary content nouns ('traffic', 'resources', 'humidity') and on 'be', 'are', 'is' inside predicates.

L20_N5444_neg.wrong_label: The same kind of token: the first fragment of a rare multi-token name or word, but with negative sign. Examples: GVSU's «Me»ijer (-6), «Me»ža prospekts (-5), Mall «Ar»tha Gading (-5), Madeleine «Re»es (-5), «Str»atford upon Avon (-5), «par»rots (-5), «Car»leton College (-5), «lo»ath (-6), thilo «sar»razin (-4), «par»quet (-3), «gre»be (-3), Rain «Sp»outs (-3). It is also negative on repository and website boilerplate. Examples: 'Full text not available «from» this repository' (-7, the strongest negative), and the Wikia ad-blocker notice, where 'Wikia' gets -2 to -3, 'modified' -3 and 'is «not» accessible' -5.

L20_N5444_pos.wrong_label: Function words that introduce the channel or platform through which an action happens: 'with' in 'Sign in with Facebook', 'using' in 'sign in using', 'on' in 'Like X on Facebook' or 'chatting on skype', 'through' in 'advertising through the radio', 'our' in 'subscribe to our channel', and commas inside lists of platforms or channels ('Instagram, Snapchat'; 'google, bing,'). Values usually run -3 to -6. The platform name that follows is often itself mildly positive.

L20_N5455_neg.wrong_label: Similarly sparse. It fires on tokens inside foreign or unusual named entities and acronyms, typically after the name has begun or at an acronym or code piece. Examples: 'ar' in Harput within a Turkish city chain (−10); 'P' in 'Iohannis – PNL' with '–' at −6 and 'Justice' at −5; 'ana' and '0' in 'Ultimasaptamana: 0' (−7, −8); 'i' in 'i5' (−7); 'O' in 'OAO' (−6); 'Maj' in Majd (−5). Other examples: 'Cad'/'and' in 'Cadence and Magma' (−4), 'al' in 'albanian' (−4), 'Required' in 'Required fields' (−5), 'special' in 'special services', 'Common' in 'Common Cranes', and 'Jim'/'George'/'Oakland' at −2 to −4. Romanian, Russian, Turkish and Albanian contexts are common, as are capitalized modifiers before a head noun.

L20_N5455_pos.wrong_label: Function words and light verbs sitting inside an ongoing, highly conventional multi-word construction, where the following words are strongly predictable. The token that carries the activation is the hinge or linking word of the frame. Examples: "as" in "as it crashes into"; "that" in "KNOWING that" or "a generally-accepted fact that"; "or" in "in whole or in part" and "customised or made to order"; "used up"; "as they relate to"; "weighs up a bid"; "trusting in God's"; "should be"; "versus"; "have a low"; "they say"; "suffering a"; "Leavy's crew". It often appears right after a subordinate "as/that/who + pronoun" opener, on the verb or the connective that follows. The hinge itself is high (6-10), and neighbouring tokens of the same phrase pick up a spread of +1 to +4.

L20_N6691_neg.wrong_label: The strong negative pole fires on activity or transaction verbs, especially buy, buying, playing, selling and do, when they are the object of a desire, start or plan construction. Examples: 'want you to start buying' (-10), 'cars they aren't buying' (-10), 'started playing' (-9), 'never playing it again' (-10), 'start selling' (-9), 'going to buy' (-9), 'didn't buy' (-8). The preceding control verb also takes a moderate negative ('want' -7, 'wants' -3). Other strong negatives: 'doi' in 'https://doi.org' (-8/-9), and Chinese instructional verbs such as 做 in 照着做 (-10) or 接 (-6). Milder hits (-3/-4) go to verbs like edit, relearn, read, cheer, and 'did' in narrative contexts.

L20_N6691_pos.wrong_label: The dominant pole. It fires on how-to text about physically working a material, mainly recipe ingredient lines and cleaning or finishing instructions. Peaks land on the manner adverb or texture participle saying how something is cut, ground, grated or scrubbed: 'finely' (-7 to -9), 'roughly' (-7), 'freshly' (-8), 'gently' (-7), 'grated' (-5 to -7), 'gr'inds' (-8), 'Scr'ubbability / 'Sc'rub (-6 to -9), lemon 'r'ind' (-5 to -10). The same descriptor in a cleaning or tool-description context also fires ('razor-sh'arp -4, 'sk'id-free -3, 'scraped with a' -3). The separator just before the descriptor in an ingredient line is also strongly negative: the comma, dash or 'and' after an ingredient noun (e.g. 'carrots,' -8, 'and' -7, 'onion,' -5, 'garlic –' -5). Lighter negatives (-1 to -3) spread over nearby ingredient nouns, measure words, and instruction words ('cup', 'tsp', 'with a', 'soft', 'dry', 'damp').

L20_N7473_pos.wrong_label: Words expressing avoiding, evading, or getting around something, such as avoid/avoiding/avoidable, steer clear of, dodged/dodging, sidestep, and navigate around. The activation sits on the verb, or on the completing particle of a phrasal verb (clear, of, around, the -ep/-pping piece of sidestep). It often carries over to the next one or two tokens that begin the avoided object: a, what, several, a comma, because. Weaker cases are related motion-around or escape senses, such as 'fled from', 'runs around a', 'drove it around a bit', and 'prevent this'.

L20_N7628_pos.wrong_label: The opening token of a quoted span or quantity whose content is a quotation, title or name. Typical cases are an opening quote mark that begins reported speech or a quoted statement after 'he said,', 'told X.', 'explained:' or 'said:' (e.g. ''If you want…'' he said, '' / "If I was…" / “We'll make mistakes”). Also opening quotes or apostrophes before organization names and titles (“We the People”, ‘Made in Japan’, ‘Abdullah’, “The Roof Clinic…”, "For his outstanding research"). Also '$' before a monetary amount ($7,500, $200, $13 billion) and the space before '21st century'. The quote or '$' token itself carries the peak (+4 to +6). The first word inside the quote often gets a smaller +1 to +4.

L20_N7718_neg.wrong_label: Same kind of translated or promotional European text, but on predicate and action parts of clauses rather than descriptive noun phrases. It fires on verbs, conjunctions, infinitive 'to', pronouns and possessives in evaluative, promotional or agentive statements. L20_N7718_pos.wrong_label: The same kind of fragment (again mostly 'f'/'F', also 'w', 'pe') when it begins a noun, proper name, or capitalized term. L20_N8730_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token just before a strongly anticipated specific named entity or technical term, in technical-support, hosting or fan-wiki contexts. Hammond", "the| Incompleteness", "The| Kh|itomer", "Robert| Carradine", "A8N|-SLI", "remote| buffer overflow", and a feature-list bullet such as "- 100". L20_N8855_pos.wrong_label: The token immediately after a digit token '7', strongest when that next token is '0'. Examples: phone area codes 7«0»3 and (7«0»8) at -10, 7«0»1-10 at -8, ZIP 7«0»345 at -7, NCC-17«0»1 at -6, 77«0»43 at -5, 7.«0» at -4, 07«0» at -2. Other followers of '7' are weaker. A hyphen after 7-then-0 (EF 70«-»300) gives about -4. 'c' after 7 inside a hex string gives about -2 to -4. The effect is mostly confined to that one token after the 7.

L20_N8902_neg.wrong_label: Words that describe a person's manner, attitude, demeanor or emotional bearing, usually in narrative or descriptive prose. Examples: self-righteous, languid, sauntered, confidently, stern, stiffly, swagger, smile, 'contented smiles', 'shock and laughter in my voice', 'like a wild beast', 'a bit sheepish', 'hysteria and exhaustion', 'easy going', lighthearted, pout, politely. The activation tends to spread at lower strength to nearby function words in the manner phrase ('a', 'and', 'with', 'like', 'up rather', 'would').

L20_N8902_pos.wrong_label: Fires at the boundary right after a short title-like or header line. It peaks on the newline token that ends a headline, product name, section title, or advisory heading, at the point where body text is about to start (e.g. 'Hydra v 7.4: Fast Network cracker↵', 'Cloud Controller API regression↵'). It also fires on header-marker words inside email or forum separators, such as 'Forwarded Mail =' in '=====Forwarded Mail=====' and 'next part' in '---- next part ----'. Weaker activations come from 'Table of Contents↵', 'Editor's Notes', and separator underscores before 'EXAMPLE'.

L20_N9319_neg.wrong_label: Fires on a token that is the opening fragment of a longer word the model expects to continue, mid-word, usually a proper noun or technical term whose completion is highly predictable. Examples: Princeton «Rep»(ertory), PH«IL»(HARMONIC), «mass»(achusetts), 1 «Th»«ess»(alonians), «FL»(ORIDA), «Cab»(ernet), Les «Mis»(érables), Eagle-T«rib»(une), «breast»(stroke), RUSSIAN F«ED»(ERATION), «rh»(inoceros), «pot»(entiometer), Army «Pam»(phlet), Trans-«App»(alachian), «Ob»«it»(uary), re«trans»(mission). L20_N9319_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that begin with or are the subword 'dr', most strongly the word 'drinking' (especially 'drinking water', 'drinking fountain', 'beer-drinking') and the bare subword 'dr' inside words or names: 'dr'+izzle, Dal+dr+up, city+dr+ift, dv+dr+help, Hy+dr+ate, well-dr+illing, dr+ystone, dr+uzzy, dr+breana. Weaker generalization covers the drinking/hydration concept and other dr- words: drinks, drunk, Dr. (title), hydration, Drive, drove, draft, dry, drop, dress.

L20_N9386_neg.wrong_label: The comma token that comes directly after the leading digit(s) of a number and is followed by more digits, as in 4,500 / $12,000 / 3,000 MW. It also fires on a European decimal comma (0,67% / € 5,08 / 3,5 µm). The activation sits on the comma itself. It is strongest when only 1–2 digits come before the comma (4, 5, 2, 3, 15, 12). When a number has several groups, later commas are weaker (5,201,3 → +9 then +3). The digit right after the comma sometimes gets about +1. Ordinary list or clause commas get weak activation (+1 to +4), most often in enumerations of nouns or names (Oldsmobile, / durable goods, / one, if not both / March 23, 201x). A stray number-like comma such as 'great, great grandson' can reach +8.

L20_N9386_pos.wrong_label: Warm, promotional or devotional praise of an in-group or identity: one's nation, region, hometown, faith or self ('our country', 'Ireland's greatest treasure', 'proudly made in England', 'how God has always been', 'I like who I am', 'how much talent we have', 'beautiful languages,', 'the wonders of biomedicine'). Activation lands on the function or possessive token that completes the proud claim ('has', 'have', 'be', 'am', 'our', ''s', ',', 'to'), and also on the place/identity noun itself ('England', 'African', 'Indian', 'country', 'Africa') or on praise nouns ('pride', 'treasures', 'wonders').

L20_N9513_neg.wrong_label: Strong, fairly specific pole: tokens that immediately precede, and set up, a mention of water or another fluid or bulk substance. The activation sits on the verb, preposition, determiner or modifier just before the fluid noun, not on the noun itself. Examples: 'pot|of|salted' before 'water'; 'bodies|of' before 'water'; 'parcel|of|surface' before 'air'; 'does not allow|the' before 'water to flow'; 'keeps|the' before 'blood flowing'; 'drops|of' before 'blood'; 'to keep' before 'drinks cold'; 'correct|transmission' before 'fluid'; 'mound|of' before 'earth'; 'out|of|the' before 'sea'; 'warm, ill-tasting' before 'water'; 'vaporizes|the' before 'nicotine'. The fluid noun itself is usually only weakly negative or zero.

L20_N9513_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token just before a head word that is predictable from earlier context, usually because it re-mentions something already discussed. Typical carriers are possessors, determiners, adjectives and fixed-phrase starters. Examples: "Apple|'s" (helper = the Siri already discussed), "jurisdiction|al" (puzzles, mentioned earlier), "these|types" (of presses), "SolarWorld|'s" (capacity), "monthly" (nut, repeated), "THUMBS-D|OWN" (mirrors THUMBS-UP), "of|ozone" (destruction, repeated), "% Daily|Value", "with" (respect to), "Pujols' former trainer|," just before the name. Also fires on a link verb or relativizer introducing info about a known entity: "The deceased|is", "the President, |who", "counsel|is".

L20_N9713_neg.wrong_label: Words expressing a sufficiency condition or an upper cap. Main cases: 'enough' in 'ADJ enough (to/that/for)' (small/close/slim/soft/quiet enough), around −4 to −6, with the following 'to' or 'that' also −2 to −5. Also 'or less' / '0 or less' / '30 minutes or less' on 'less' (−3 to −6), and 'and under' for age or price caps (−5).

L24_N0162_neg.wrong_label: Distributive or multiplicative counting, where a number applies to each member or to items in an itemized list rather than to one joint group. Examples: 'each for two nights)' (−10 on the ')'), 'three couples' (−7), 'by each party,' (−5/−6), 'three, two-bedroom flats' (−6 on 'two'), '3 lunches and 3 dinners' (−5 on the second '3'), 'on both Saturday…' (−5), 'two sets of' (−5 on 'of'), 'every two miles' (−4), 'fourth and eighth grade' (−3/−4), '20 characters', '(3″)', list colons and line breaks in spec or inventory lists. Activation lands on the number, 'each', 'every', 'of', closing punctuation, or a newline right after a per-unit quantity.

L24_N0162_pos.wrong_label: Other words that begin with ac/acc but are unrelated to accreditation: the ap/ella pieces of "acapella", "accordion", Acacia, Akola, the acco pieces of "accoPlus", accolades, carpaccio, Acronis. These are the neuron pushing away the wrong "ac-" word. They sit around -1 to -6, and the strongest is acapella.

L24_N0202_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the surname or name-word that forms part of a local, proper-named facility or location. These are names honoring a person, or obscure place names, sitting right before or inside 'Stadium/Theatre/Park/Library/Gymnasium/Award/Society/Avenue/Road/Building/Street'. Examples: Homer→Scott Stadium (−10); John D→utton Theatre (−7); Len→Howard Conservation Park (−7); Pret→low Branch Library (−7); East→Main Media Studios (−6); Lund→holm Gymnasium; Barbara J→ordan essay competition; James E.→Sullivan Award; Theresa→Palmer Society; Loh→man Avenue; Cog→bill Rd; Sham→rock Road; Humph→rey Building; Des→oto Street; Mamas→apan. It does not fire on the generic facility noun itself (≈−1 at most). Rare form-text cases also occur, e.g. 'contact→information' (−5).

L24_N1387_neg.wrong_label: The dominant pole. It fires strongly on the verb 'begin' and its inflections: begin, Begin, BEGIN, begins, began, at -8 to -10. This includes sentence-initial imperatives ('Begin training'), 'BEGIN PGP SIGNED', and phrases like 'the process begins' or 'Obama began promoting'. The noun 'beginning' is weaker, around -4 to -5. Related start words are weaker still: 'start' about -2, 'started' about -1. The token right after can carry a small negative: 'with' or 'of' at -1 to -3, and 'to' after 'started' at about -3.

L24_N1387_pos.wrong_label: Tokens inside a phrase describing something ending or stopping, especially the main verb of an idiom that predicts 'to an end / to a close / to a halt' or 'ended'. L24_N1872_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that name or point to a physical or abstract location as the spot where something exists, stands, is put, or substitutes for something else. The biggest peak is on the head noun 'site' in phrases like 'the trade center site' or 'at the site' (+7 to +10). 'where'/'wherever' clauses fire on 'where' and on the following existential verb or article ('where there is a well', 'where the webcam would normally be'). Substitution frames fire on 'in place of', 'in its place a', and 'replace'. Location-filling verbs fire too: 'filled that house', 'stood on what had been a', 'now stands', 'leaving only', 'fill in imperfections'. Other spatial nouns such as spot, ground, pit, and center also count. Activation often peaks on the token that completes the locative slot ('site', 'ground', 'be', 'would', 'stands', 'a' after 'had been'/'there is').

L24_N1953_neg.wrong_label: The 'www' token right after 'http://' or 'https://' in a URL, about +5 to +7, and the same in every such URL. The preceding 'http' gets about +1. Domain endings ('.com', '.edu', '.org') can get +1 to +3. Weaker positives (+2 to +6) go to web-page boilerplate and front-matter words: 'Copyright', '©', 'Table of Contents', 'Contents', 'Book Description', 'disclaimer', 'Bestselling Author', and '@example.com'. A bare 'www' with no 'http://' in front gets only about +1.

L24_N1953_pos.wrong_label: The head noun of a noun phrase naming people, or an entity treated like an agent (customers, businesses, owner, members, folks, spectators, others, provider, family, store, designer, person, CEO, players, students), especially when it is the thing obtained, built, served or started. Typical frames: 'obtain new customers', 'buys ... businesses', 'found a new owner', 'started a business', 'using others', 'build successful businesses', 'a much-hyped store', 'family drama/recipes/gathering', 'modern designer rug'. The activation sits on the noun itself, usually right after an adjective or modifier ('new', 'successful', 'service', 'family', 'Corps'). The word 'family' used as a modifier also fires (+6).

L24_N2997_pos.wrong_label: The final subword fragment that completes a long multi-token word after a short opening fragment. This is common in ALL-CAPS text, URLs/domains and proper names. L24_N3339_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that act as structural or navigational chrome attached to a section heading. L24_N3702_neg.wrong_label: Subword tokens that end in the letter t/T and leave the word unfinished, so the next token must continue it. L24_N3702_pos.wrong_label: Mild positive (+1 to +4) on the words of a qualifying condition or threshold that describes who or what something applies to. Examples: "more than two other people working together", "properties over 1 story", "kids under 10", "between the ages of 14 and 19", "50 seconds left on the clock", "how long they have been exposed", "progressed enough in both diseases", "when one party has a", "depending on how far you live from", "the low RDS(ON)".

L24_N3708_pos.wrong_label: Promotional or enthusiast lifestyle prose about food, wine, sake, art, crafts, fragrance, design or gifts. The activation lands on the connector or function token that sets up the next category noun: '&', 'and', ',', 'of', 'for', 'with', 'about', '/', '-made', '-course', '-based'. L24_N3838_pos.wrong_label: Also on tokens inside structured or templated strings, but in different templates. L24_N4800_pos.wrong_label: First subword token of an unfamiliar, usually foreign proper name (most often a surname) that the tokenizer splits into pieces.
