Examples: Sils«bee», Trent«ino»/Trent«o», Ad«ige», Egg«ental», P«iz», Var«ese», Mint«urn», Wals«all», Véz«elay», Castor«zza», Mö«lle», Molenbe«ek», Bellag«io». The first token of the name is usually weak. The strongest values fall on later fragments that complete an exotic name. Common words and well-known names give near zero.

L24_N6939_neg.wrong_label:
Sparse and idiosyncratic, mostly in boilerplate or technical text.
- Strongest: the word 'for' in the Wikia notice 'We have a modified experience for viewers using ad blockers' (≈ -9). In that notice, 'using' ≈ -2, '!\n' ≈ -1 to -2, and 'experience' and '-to' are mildly positive (+1).
- Odd name fragments, e.g. 'omed' in Iomedae (-9), 'utt' in Guttormsson (-4).
- Newlines or periods ending a patent claim or software-doc paragraph before a new numbered or instruction line (-8).
- ':"' before a pasted log line (-8), 'Message:' (-5).
- 'when' in a definitional sentence ('pressure in arteries when your heart beats', -8).
- ',' in ad copy ('each month, you'll get', -8).
- Also milder: ':\n' before a bulleted list (-4), and '.\n' or '.' ending an expository paragraph (-2 to -3).

L24_N6939_pos.wrong_label: Neutral or benign purpose/goal verbs, and the words right after them, in 'used to X' or 'in order to X' frames. Examples: 'to avoid', 'to update', 'to improve', 'to manage', 'to maintain', 'to review', 'to protect', 'to correct', 'to balance', 'Prevention', 'control'. Universal quantifiers after such verbs or prepositions also fire ('all of', 'with all', 'to all'). So do some value nouns: 'reminder', 'average', 'additional', 'granted' (as in 'take for granted'), 'frowned on'. These are mostly constructive, administrative or helpful actions.

L24_N7364_pos.wrong_label:
Content words, mostly nouns, plus some core verbs like learn/think/see/move, used as generic kind or concept terms when a passage explains how the world works or what something fundamentally is. Typical settings: science or educational explanation, definitions and philosophical asides, and category lists of exemplars.

Peak examples:
- "the idea of infinity" → infinity
- "every time we learn something new" → learn
- "how we think" → think
- "IP address" → address
- "'living' and 'conscious'" → each word
- "roles of light energy and carbon dioxide" → light
- "gravity is still gravity" → second gravity
- "the light we see" → see
- "Fruit Item: Apple, Orange, Banana" → Orange
- "visible to the human eye" → eye
- "from robin's eggs to quasars" → quasars
- "carbon atoms" → atoms
- "principles of life" → life
- "the nature of men / women" → men, women

The activation lands on the concept word itself, usually the head noun or a key verb. Modifiers before it get smaller values (human +2–4, carbon +4, ultr-aviolet +6, Internet +7).

L24_N7907_pos.wrong_label: The same kinds of opening tokens when the span is a short UI label, an imperative command, a slogan, or a single word or term being mentioned. Examples are button names (click the “Get it” / “Sign in” / "Open File" button), voice commands (“Find Nearest…”), shirt slogans ("Wife to One") and words being defined (and 'masturbate'). Also an opening quote before a yelled imperative (yells, "Hey kid, get…") and a colon in transcript dialogue right before a short reply (Me: Yes…). Also the space or digit opening a day-of-month in a date (born on 22nd May; October 25th). These reach −5 to −10, carried by the quote mark, colon or space token.

L24_N8414_neg.wrong_label: Tokens in number/count constructions, especially a digit or word naming a figure or shape, or the noun right after a small count word. Examples: 'figure 8' → '8' −10; 'Figure-8s' → '8' −9, 's' −5; 'Solution 1' → '1' −6; 'Around 23' → '2' −6; 'Three-vehicle collision' → '-' −4, 'collision' −6; 'three-layer' → 'three' −6; 'the three forms' → 'three' −5. A few other content tokens in formal or academic phrasing also go negative: 'Consistency conditions' → −7, 'Steadman' → −6, 'solution structures' → −5, 'for the customer' → 'the' −5, 'from Troy' → −5. Inside random ID strings the sign can flip: 'hi' in …Me0hiT → −9. Clock times ('6:51', '8:45') give −2 to −3 on the ':' and the following digit.

L24_N9132_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that open a slot where new, specific descriptive content is about to follow. Typical cases: a subject plus auxiliary or verb that introduces a description or attribute ("the words| stay", "These items| have| never", "floors| are|/can", "Russell is described| as", "police| will"). Also purpose or lead-in markers like "to write| a", "In addition| to", "onto which| we'll| hand|write", "codes| for", "being| of". Also list/spec scaffolding in descriptive or listing text: "what you'll| learn|:", "opportunity to:↵|-", dashes or newlines starting the next amenity ("garage↵–"), commas between adjectives in hotel/property blurbs ("comfortable, clean, modern rooms"), and numeric fields in specs, timestamps or page numbers ("Slipcase 30 x 20", "T14:25:33", "Page 1679", "(0.004 inch)"). Common genres are property/product/hotel blurbs, announcements and expository definitions.

L24_N9132_pos.wrong_label:
The strong pole. It fires on the main predicate verb, or its completing particle, when that verb is an action or change-of-state verb. The verb usually follows 'will', 'to', 'might', 'has', or 'that' and denotes a process of change: maintain, improve, increase, unlock, stall, sign, unmask, cool (down), turn off, melt away, ramp up, bring in, carry out.
- In phrasal verbs the particle often carries the peak: 'turns off' (off −7), 'melts away' (away −7), 'ramping up' (up −6), 'carry out' (out −4).
- Milder cases (−1 to −3) are passive or past participles used as predicates: issued, made, introduced, tracked, used, established.

L24_N9347_neg.wrong_label: Fires on titles and organizational/institutional descriptors in non-US-electoral, formal, or foreign settings. Examples: 'Mayor' in 'Milwaukee Mayor Tom Barrett' (-9), 'Divisional' in 'Divisional Commander/Magistrate' (-6, -3), and Spanish/foreign institution names ('Diputación Foral de' -3 to -5). Also hit are lists of officials or bodies ('the Chief Justice', 'the National Council', -4 to -5) and Indigenous nation lists ('Dene, Lakota', -4/-5). Some byline 'by' tokens and name fragments also go negative (-3 to -5).

L24_N9451_pos.wrong_label: Fires on a token that sits inside a specific named entity, title or memorized quote, where earlier context already commits to that one entity. It usually lands on the 2nd or later piece of the name, often a sub-word fragment. Examples: Øyaf|estival|en, Mike Mai|olo, Stefan Moly|neux, Sylvia Bo|orstein, Chimamanda Ngo|zi, jillc|imore|lli, vmkfst|ools. It also hits the next word of a known multiword name or title: Official Code of Georgia, Bradford Park Avenue, Center for Cognitive Liberty, The Impossible Knife (of Memory), Yorkshire Sculpture Park, NHK WORLD, The Simpsons Tapped Out, Gamecube … Wii, Red Cross shelters, WordPress.com stats (helper monkeys), Dawn Treader, Creedence Clearwater, Bethesda Soft(works), Abbot Kinney. It fires on famous quote continuations too: "Gratitude unlocks the fullness…" = top activation.

L24_N9595_neg.wrong_label: A preposition, or occasionally a conjunction or comma, that links a verb or noun of physical placement, motion, contact, or containment to a location or object NP. Examples: nest under, hitting the, meander through, winds through, surrounded by, set amongst, up in the trees, protected by the, loosen the, remove and discard, with an adjacent, shallow open water, mudflats and. Peaks of -7 to -10 land on the preposition or action word. The following 'the/a' often gets -4 to -6. Similes like 'white as wool' and 'where she loves to be' also fire negatively.

L24_N9595_pos.wrong_label: The neuron fires positively in technical, scientific and product prose at the first token of a specific identifier or value that pins down a referent. Examples: an open parenthesis or first character of an abbreviation, strain or cell line ('(E. coli', '(HMEC', '(EMBOSS'); catalog numbers ('(#9998', strongest on the middle digits); citation volume or year digits ('no. 39 (2'); and a range's start year ('from 2019', fires on '2'). It also fires weakly on protocol words such as 'elution', 'mM' and 'fold a protein', and on some name fragments ('Peresz-te-gi', 'Çele-bi', 'Colleen'). Outside science it fires weakly on boilerplate function words: 'we' in website disclaimers, 'your' in terms of service, Bible verse numbers.

L28_N0257_neg.wrong_label: Interior parts of a number rather than its leading digit: the decimal point and the digits after a leading '1' in metric values. Examples: '/ 1.359 m' (the '.' reaches −10, the '1' about −4), '5’3”/1.60m' (−4/−3), '21.6 cm' (the '.' about −3), '/ 10.7' (the '1' about −5). Also middle digits of long identifiers or years ('7,266,20' patent number, the 6 at −9; '(1973)', the 7 at −4). There are occasional weak negatives (−2) on name fragments such as 'Ljungqvist' and 'Breman'.

L28_N0257_pos.wrong_label: The second or third subword piece of an unusual proper name, username, or rare word when the model is completing or recognizing a previously seen name rather than reading random characters. Examples: almot|ri|ptan (-6), j|inx|nit55 (-5/-4), Fc|ON|SiX (-5), k|1|Ng0r (-5), Gle|am|Tech (-5/-3), d|re|amees (-5), z|ill (-3/-4), Qu|ir|ky (-3/-4), Q|uby (-4), Horn|wood (-4), Wich|ans|ky (-3). This is strongest on a repeated mention of a name seen earlier in the text.

L28_N0865_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token 'afford' (as in 'can afford', 'can't afford', 'least afford') and 'affordable' (also misspelled 'af|ordable'). The activation sits on that word token itself, and it fires at full strength whether the sense is financial ('a price you can afford', 'affordable health care') or idiomatic ('cannot afford to miss'). Weaker spillover: (1) unrelated words that start with the 'aff' subword token, such as Daff(odil), giffgaff, affix, Affair, -affirming, STAFFORD, affidavit, at about +2 to +3; (2) other cheapness or price words, such as 'cheap', 'cheaper', 'least expensive', 'budget', 'prices' right after 'affordable', at about +1.

L28_N1239_neg.wrong_label: Fragment tokens that start with T/t followed by a vowel, mostly 'To', 'Te', 'Ti', 'to', 'oto', 'ata', inside names or rare words that continue. Examples: "O'To|ole" (-4 to -5), 'myc-oto-xinivorans' (-3), 'TO|YBOX', 'Nick-to-ons', 'Te|lemann', 'Te|versal', 'ti|ara', 'To|peka', 'To|SIA', 'Hukk-ata-ival' (about -2).

L28_N1249_neg.wrong_label: Content words of a short title-case heading or subheading that appears on its own line after a paragraph of body text, e.g. 'Innovation Still Has a Ways to Go', 'Better Safe Than Sorry', 'Invest in the Best', 'Price War in Imported Assault Weapons', 'Trick Your Brain Into…', 'ROGERS MAKING STRIDES'. It fires on tokens after the first word of the heading, peaks on the second to fourth word (the key noun or verb, such as Still/has, Revolution, Reliability, World, Best, Foundation, Value, Here, Out), and often carries onto the newline that ends the heading. It is strongest for catchy, idiomatic or slogan-like headings in blog, article or marketing prose.

L28_N1249_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token that finishes a familiar multi-token unit. Examples: the title word that closes a known name ("All Is Well" peaks on "Well", +10); a head noun after a modifier ("generic version" +7, "longtime companion" +4, "any extras" +4, "boom beach" +4); and inner digits of phone numbers or quantities ("21"1 +4, "162"→"2" +4, "750" on "5" +4). It also fires weakly on function words that come right after a clause or subject ("calling it" +5, "sequences at" +4, "Savings and" +4, "they had" +4, "This product" +3–4). There is no single clear semantic theme.

L28_N1371_neg.wrong_label: Tokens inside a clause that echoes information the addressee or user has already supplied, used as a known premise for a reply or inference. Typical frames: "since you are flying to Paris on TAM", "since you said", "(you in this scenario)", "What you say you're looking for is", "you have opted to", "You are searching for", "as is your requirement", "Detail provided for", "The part \"...\" of the query". Activation peaks on the verb, preposition or noun that completes the stated premise, just before the new content or conclusion: on (+10), are (+7), scenario (+7), is (+7), have (+7), searching (+6), said (+5), requirement (+5). It weakly generalizes to any given or specified parameter being anchored: "at boot", "at a price point of", "when the snow begins", "hit only once", "actually 0,67", "for your smaller gathering".

L28_N1371_pos.wrong_label: Subordinators that open an attendant-circumstance or condition clause describing what state something is in while an action happens: 'while', 'when', 'with' (as in 'with the key on'), and 'in (situ)'. They appear mostly in technical, instructional or product text, e.g. 'carried out with the ADR in situ', 'room available when the rear seat is folded', 'look at the vent while the dryer is on', 'push down on the vehicle while it's parked', 'fuse 22 is only hot with the key on', 'when relaxed', 'when standing upright', 'when equipped with', 'with the speed 12', 'while recording', 'while you are on this page'. The connective itself carries the peak. The next one or two tokens of the clause stay moderately positive, typically the subject or determiner ('the', 'it', '’s', 'you are'). A secondary weaker pattern is imperative instruction starts in how-to lists, e.g. '- Make sure', 'Measure the', 'Place one', 'Put back', 'Leave on'.

L28_N1389_neg.wrong_label: Text set in statistics, econometrics or the R language. The strongest firing is on R package-page boilerplate such as "Package repository | View on GitHub | Install the latest version of this package by entering the following in R: Add the following code to...". There, nearly every token is high (+5 to +10), with peaks on "View", newline/"Install", ":" before code, and "Add". Weaker, diffuse firing (+1 to +4) occurs across statistics writing: Bayesian/likelihood jargon (posteriors, prior distribution, reparametrizations, likelihood), MCMC, econometrics citations (Hansen, Johansen, cointegration, Journal of Econometrics, RePEc pages), statistician names (Koopman, Ljung), SAS discussion lists, "So You Need to Learn R", years in citations of statistics papers, and probability calculations.

L28_N1389_pos.wrong_label: The token " (" (space + open paren) when it follows a noun phrase and opens a descriptive gloss, specification, abbreviation, or qualifier for that noun. Strongest after academic degree names ("B. Sc (Hons)", "M.Sc (Geology)", "BA (modern history)", "Bachelor of Arts (B.A.)", "Thesis (Other)"). Also fires for an institution or name followed by its acronym ("Monash Art Design & Architecture (MADA)"), script speaker tags ("RICHARD (SYNC)"), botanical or term glosses ("bracts (phyllaries)", "hermaphrodite (has both...)"), quantity specs ("1 package (8 ounces)"), name glosses ("LITTLE GIRL (Wyncie)"), and source tags ("(DS9:"). The activation sits on the paren token itself. The first token inside sometimes gets a small +1 to +3.

L28_N1795_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token 'organizations' / 'organisations', the plural noun meaning institutions or groups. It is strongest on the plural, at about +8 to +10, regardless of context: Islamist, allied, health care, government, faith-based and so on. The singular 'organization' / 'organisation' gets about +5 to +7. 'tissues' also fires strongly (+8 to +9), both for biological tissue and for facial tissues, most likely a shared 'organ-'/plural-noun lexical feature. Weaker hits: the verb forms 'organize' / 'organized' / 'organised' at +3 to +5, 'Organization' in a title such as 'Table of Organization' at about +3, 'networks' / 'network' at +2 to +3. Collective nouns like 'groups', 'community' and 'structure', and words like 'conduct', 'tightening' and 'Islamist' near the noun, get about +1.

L28_N2161_neg.wrong_label: Spanish (and Filipino-Spanish) proper names embedded in English or Spanish text, with the activation on the opening token of the name. Strongest on articles and possessives that begin a name: «La», «Los», «Las», «El», «Nuestra», «del», «de la», «dela». Also strong on the first piece of a Spanish surname or place name after a first name or title: «S»ánchez -9, «P»ampa -4, «Tep» -6, «Com»edor -6, «B»ú -6, «N»ueva -6. Examples: «La» Hosteria -8, «La» guerra -10, «N»uestra Salud -10, Mar «del» Plata -1. Later pieces of the same name can flip slightly positive (+1 to +3).

L28_N2161_pos.wrong_label: Fires just before or on names in Greek, Balkan, Polish, Bulgarian or Middle-East contexts, often on the connective that introduces the name. Examples: 'novel of' → Apostolos (-9), 'King' Tomislav (-9), 'outskirts of' a Cypriot village (-8), 'director,' (-8), 'Polish director' Andrzej (-8/-6), Stanimir (-8), Anastassios Pouris (-7/-6), 'Boris'ov (-7), 'President' Bashar (-7), 'named' John Huss (-7), 'father,' (-7), year tokens in biographies (-7). The role nouns director, president and father, plus 'of', 'named', 'in' and commas that introduce a foreign personal or place name, carry the negative value.

L28_N2863_neg.wrong_label: Strongest on the name token 'Lucas' in any use: person names (Lucas Neill), 'Lucas county', 'Lucasfilm', 'Lucas's'. These reach -6 to -10. Moderate negatives (-3 to -5) fall on evaluative adjectives placed before a noun: 'impossible' (quest, enemy, choices, Knife), 'useful' (tools, products), 'difficult' (conversations), 'necessary' (supplies). The odd name fragment also fires (e.g. 'sarah' → -4). Mild -1 values appear on similar adjectives such as potential, vital, relevant, meaningful, effective.

L28_N2863_pos.wrong_label: Function and connective tokens in, or right next to, Romance-language or Latin text and Hispanic/Latin names. Typical triggers are commas, 'de', 'la', 'y', 'or', '(' and auxiliaries like 'estão'/'están'. The activation lands on the connective token that links two foreign items or opens a foreign phrase. Examples: list comma 'Taza, or Abuelita' (+9); 'N° de référence' ('de' +7); 'Caminos, Canales y Puertos' (',' +6, 'y' +5); 'Nuestra' (+5); 'freelancers están/estão' (+4); Latin loan phrases in English ('ad interim', 'sui generis', 'ad' and 'sui' about +4); Romance-looking name pieces ('Benaud' 'ena' +3/+4, 'Simona' 'ona' +3, 'Pujols' 'uj' +3). Weak activations (+1 to +2) are scattered across Spanish/Portuguese prose, especially on articles, prepositions and nouns.

L28_N3518_neg.wrong_label: Personal names in bibliographic author lists, especially the initials and surname pieces right after a comma in 'Surname, X., Surname, Y.' or 'Surname AB, Surname CD' sequences. The strongest responses are on initials ('C' -10, 'HT' -9, 'KE' -8), given names after a surname-comma ('Lars' -9), and the trailing commas (-5). Weaker negatives come from author names before 'wrote' in email quotes, and from usernames.

L28_N3518_pos.wrong_label: Tokens in the middle of a formal identifier or reference string, especially after a designator that tells the reader a specific code or path is coming. The identifier tokens themselves fire, not the designator. Examples: journal volume and page numbers (Phys. Rev. B 71553), patent numbers (U.S. patent 7,266,205), statute and regulation numbers (MINN. STAT. 176.2; 50 CFR 40; Title 17; Stats. 2001), SIC codes, FreeBSD/CVS paths (usr/ports/X11, ports/security, pgsql-server/src/backend), category paths (category "Antiques\Furniture"; Subjects: | R Medicine > R), and UI navigation steps (go to the File menu; click on; choose). Activation is strongest a few tokens into a numeric or path sequence. The peak is the 3rd–5th digit of a citation number (~+10).

Tokens inside formulaic, memorized, or template-like text, where the next tokens are strongly predictable from familiar web or code boilerplate. The activation lands on the token just before the predictable continuation. Examples:

- 'Funding«:» This work was supported'
- 'itunes«.apple».com/us/«album»/'

- 'enter the following «command»:'

These are code keywords, URL paths, legal/academic boilerplate, and stock phrases.

L28_N3610_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token "set" and its inflections ("sets", "setting", "Set"), including when it is the second half of a compound (hand|sets, Fact|Set, skill|set, trend|setting). It covers every sense: noun meaning a collection (train set, sheet sets, drum set, a set of), verb uses (set out, set up, set a deadline, stage is set, sets him bemoaning), and participle/descriptive uses (Set in apartheid-era South Africa, set against). The activation sits on the "set" token itself. The next token (out, of) sometimes gets a small +1 to +2.

L28_N3639_neg.wrong_label: First-person or customer-addressed narratives about physically relocating or travelling. Examples: 'friends moving back from out of', 'moving abroad', 'move it all back in', 'on my trip to Geneva', 'Your Next Trip', 'professional moving of your household goods', 'we are moving this weekend… living out of our cars', 'drove my mother to'. Negative values land on the motion verb ('moving', 'move', 'moved', 'drove'), and on the possessives, prepositions and travel nouns around it ('my', 'on', 'of', 'our', 'next', 'trip', 'from', 'the'). The same pattern appears weakly for upcoming personal events and visits: 'my next visit', 'an unforgettable Event', 'after a major renovation'.

L28_N3768_pos.wrong_label: Strong (down to −10). Fires where text attributes opinions or experiences to other people, as in reviews, testimonials, owner reports and user submissions. The largest values land on the noun naming the third-party group: "Some owners find" (−10 on "owners"), "Owners note" (−4), "used by a customer" (−4), "a KDE Plasma user" (−5 on "user"). Attribution frames also fire: "Submitted by NAME", "From: Tanner:", "Comments:", "Customer Raves & Reviews", "u/llorca336 gave", "feedback from", "delegates had to say", "we're chiming in", "Chapter will hold". The first token of the quoted testimonial that follows is also strongly negative: "I" or "“I" (−5 to −6), ""This" (−5), and "!↵" ending a review (−5). Usernames and the newlines in these attribution lines get −1 to −3.

L28_N3802_pos.wrong_label: The full words 'Certified/certified', 'certification(s)', 'certifying' and 'Recertified', marking a professional or product credential status. The activation sits on the word token itself, or on the suffix token 'ified'/'ifying'/'IFIED' after a separate 'cert' token. It is strongest in credential phrases: 'Salesforce Certified Platform Developer' (-10), 'Certified Public Accountant', 'board certified specialist', 'Certified Used Vehicles', 'Factory Recertified', 'CE-certified' (-4 to -8). 'certification' in process or requirement contexts gives -3 to -4. Related words are weakly negative: 'credentialing' (-1 to -2), 'accreditation' (-2), 'qualified', 'recognized', 'Specialist' and 'License' (around -1).

L28_N4337_neg.wrong_label:
The strong pole. It fires on the content word itself, the adjective or noun token, not the words around it. Two overlapping families:
(1) Latinate words beginning with 'pro-', especially prolific (-9 to -10), prohibit/prohibitions (-7/-8; the first subword 'prohib' is strongest and '-itions' gets about -4), proliferation (-7), progenitor (-4); 'reproduction' (-7) also counts.
(2) Adjectives of elaborate complexity, intensity or unwieldiness: intricate (-7/-8), cumbersome (-7), vigorous (-7), complicated (-4).
Weaker negatives (-1 to -4) go to related descriptors and quantity words: frequent/frequenting (-4), fewer (-4), extensively, stubborn, complex, likely, hardly. Some proper-noun subwords also get -1 to -3 (Norfolk, Bashar, Zopor-, Soph).

L28_N4468_neg.wrong_label: Result or consequence predicates and linkers that follow a condition or comparison. Verbs: 'signifies', 'making', 'will yield', 'produces', 'has', 'prove to be incorrect'. Linkers: 'and' after 'take out any of these factors', 'than' or 'from' after 'different', 'whether'. Degree and loss words: 'no longer', 'significantly lower', 'lack completely'. The common thread is the point where a stated cause or difference is cashed out as an outcome.

L28_N4468_pos.wrong_label: Strongest on the word 'sail' in all its forms: sail, sails, sailing, Sail, the 'ail' piece of Sailors or Sunsail, and the 'sail' in sailboat. These reach about +7 to +9 in boating or travel contexts. Weaker, scattered positives fall on the content noun that ends a compound and names concrete equipment or products: -tight (weather-tight) +7, food 'trucks' or 'ies' (foodies) +6/+7, clothes'lines' +7, egg 'y'(olk) +7, Japanese 的な after 論理 +9, package/boxes/ship +3/+4. Words following 'sail' (boat, rig, schedule, Area) get only +1 to +2.

L28_N4632_pos.wrong_label: Clauses in consumer, service or commercial prose that describe what a customer gets out of a transaction or service: how much value per payment ('less fuel for your money', 'more burn for your buck', 'the full price', 'full refund'), how long service takes or when it happens ('took forever to get the food', 'take too long to get a load', 'allow a few extra days for us to order this before sending it out', 'get back to you with more information', 'get the work back to me'), and whether things work or perform as expected ('refrigerators no longer seem to work efficiently', 'it just doesn't fit', 'ready and willing to help'). Activation builds across the phrase and peaks on mid-phrase function or relation words: 'for', 'before', 'to', 'with', 'back', 'the', 'longer', 'by' (as in '100 pellets by box'). The noun after the peak is usually lower.

L28_N5443_neg.wrong_label: Strong. The main trigger is the digits of the day number inside dates: 'September 2|2', 'August 1|2th', '2010-02-0|5', '2013-07-2|5', 'Jul 2|6', 'May 2|0|1|4'. The digit token that begins or forms the day gets about −7 to −10, and year digits sometimes get −2 to −7. A space token right before a day number ('October ␣23') also gets about −4 to −6. A secondary trigger is fragments of brand, company or proper names, often foreign: N|ortel −7, Mo|eller −6, Su|ja −6, FX −6, non-K|eny −6, Saf|ar|icom −2, Ar|tha −3. Location and venue contexts get weaker values (−1 to −3), such as the Big 12 name itself (−1 to −3) and '-seat'.

L28_N5443_pos.wrong_label: Tokens inside descriptive category or superlative phrases that set up a genre, industry or ranking noun. Examples: 'one of the biggest [law firms] in [Cyprus]', 'the largest debut funds in the growth company segment', 'most popular philosophy show in the world' (with 'in' and 'the' around -4 to -5), 'the American punk', 'pop punk', 'adult power ballads', 'Top Ten Articles'. Also fires on some proper-name or rare-word starts: 'Cor|inne' -7, 'chees|ecloth' -6, 'Tr|icubes' -5. Values are typically -2 to -7.

L28_N5461_pos.wrong_label: The 'bowl' family in the cricket/bowling sense fires strongest on the suffix token after 'bow': 'bowled' gives -10, 'bowlers'/'bowler' -5 to -8, 'bowling' -5 to -7. Whole-word 'bowling' or 'bowls' gives about -3 to -5. L28_N7123_neg.wrong_label: Fires on the token(s) of the lexeme 'use' when it is used as a noun or names a person: 'user(s)' (multi-user, road users, Highway Users, Natural User Interface, User comments, new users), 'usage(s)', 'use' as a noun (fair use, social use, any other use, the use of, effective use of), and especially 'disuse'/'disused'. L28_N7123_pos.wrong_label: Nouns and verbs naming the target outcome of an effort to influence or acquire people. The clearest cases are business-growth results: sales, leads, customers, traffic, clicks, conversions, acquisition and business. It also covers non-commercial persuasion targets such as recruitment, getting someone to drink, encouraging people to join, and having an effect. The neuron fires inside purpose or result phrases like "increase/boost/drive/get more X", "to encourage X", "get the reader to buy" and "convert the sale". The peak lands on the outcome word (sales, leads, customers, recruitment, converting). Neighbouring tokens in the same phrase light up more moderately: the intensifiers more and increase, the infinitive to, and and in coordinated lists.

L28_N7381_neg.wrong_label: Concrete food-ingredient nouns in recipe, menu, or dish descriptions, especially meats and cheeses. The activation sits on the ingredient token itself, or on the final subword of a split word. Strongest cases: 'chicken' (BBQ chicken, marinated chicken, chicken wings, cream of chicken), 'cheese', 'Cheddar'/'cheddar', 'fontina', 'pork', 'bbq', 'chees(ey)'. Weaker on modifiers and other ingredients in the same list: grilled, shredded, melted, Swiss, beef, sauerkraut, pineapple, basil, ribs. Rare weak hits occur on prepositions in product descriptions ('come in a', 'clamps on to').

L28_N7381_pos.wrong_label: Strong. Fires inside short, verbless, evaluative or comment fragments that follow a description or anecdote. These are informal asides and reviews like "Delicious.", "Not bad", "All impressive stuff, but", "Easy peasy, right?", "A tale for another time, but", "My kind of guy.", "A great event;", "Convenient,", "Inane, but catchy", "Cumbersome and redundant.", "Craziness but", "Very cute!", "All in all", "Pretty much a". Activation is largest on the evaluative word (bad, Delicious, stuff, peasy) and on the punctuation or conjunction that ends or pivots the fragment ("," "." ";" "but" "right" "what"). The pivot "but" after such a fragment is often the peak (-6 to -10).

L28_N7695_neg.wrong_label: Tokens of the lexeme 'shape' in any sense: shape, shapes, shaped, shaping, Shape. This covers physical form ('shape of your eyebrows', 'Mat Shape: Round'), the verb meaning to influence ('shape the future'), 'shaping up to be', 'in the best shape', and '-shaped' compounds. It also fires on the subword 'Sh'+'ap' pieces, as in 'Shapely' or the place name 'Shap'. Activation sits on the shape token itself. The following token ('of', 'up', 'like', 'and', '&', 'your') often gets a small +1 to +4 echo.

L28_N7695_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the first subword token of an uncommon proper name that is split into several pieces, mostly surnames and place names. Gaelic 'Mc'/'Mac' prefixes are typical, as in 'Mc|Leod', 'Mc|Eachran', 'Mac|leod Trail' and 'Mac Thornberry'. Indian and other foreign place names also trigger it ('Ch|alisgaon', 'P|ottstown', 'M|uleshoe', 'Kom|bo', 'P|lovdiv'), as do names like 'Ak|ers' and 'Ak|ashi'. The activation sits on the initial fragment, and later fragments are near 0. It is stronger when the name appears in a list or after a title or role such as 'by', 'Reps.', or 'Hon.'.

L28_N7708_neg.wrong_label: Mainly fires on the first or middle subword piece of an uncommon proper noun or coined word that is being spelled out piece by piece. Examples: J«ol»iet, Sn«az»zy, Proenza Sch«ou»ler, «Trig»lav, «Ar»jel, «Reb»ello, «Robin»ho, DiN«ap»oli, «Bol»zano, Yar«nev», «Cool» Buck (a game title), Cool Edit. The activation sits on the piece that opens or continues the name, not on its final piece. Also strong on an email/forum subject prefix "Re" ("Re:"). A weaker, diffuse positive (+1 to +6) appears in explanatory or question-style prose about methods, math or software. Typical hits are the function word or verb before the topic noun: "To evaluate| the", "in| computer| algebra", "understand| multiplication| and", "subtract|ing", "calculated member's", "asking for bad".

L28_N8375_neg.wrong_label: Verbs (and their following particles/objects) for sudden, rapid, forceful propulsive motion: whip, shoot/shot (literal gunfire or figurative 'shot to fame', 'prices shot up', 'shoot your mouth off', 'shoot the bull'), fire/rifle a shot past someone, dart out, burst outward, whiplash, quick fire. Activation often peaks on the verb or the next word (to, up, your, past, the head) and spills onto the following particle or object at +1 to +2.

L28_N8375_pos.wrong_label: Fires on a concrete transitive action verb, or on the determiner right after it, at the point where a direct object is expected. Typical verbs involve physically handling or placing things: put, place, cover, pour, coil, hang, fill, stick, install, combine, pair, warm, light, cut, power, use, turn, glaze, dress. The largest values (+4 to +5) usually sit on the article or determiner just after the verb ('shine «a»', 'Cover «the»', 'Pour «the»', 'cut «a»', 'coiled «the»'). Values are also large on the verb itself when the object comes next ('to «place»', 'we «installed»', 'to «power»', 'to «fill»', 'we «warmed»'). Following particles or prepositions that set up a location for the object get +1 to +4 ('stuck a tube «in»', 'Photoshopped a watch «off»', 'rope «on»'). Infinitival 'to' or the subject 'We' just before such a verb gets about +1.

L28_N9213_neg.wrong_label: Named entities, especially well-known brands, products, software, franchises, sports teams and US cities/regions. Examples: Voicemail (the '-icemail' token), Illustrator, Anaheim, Fairfax, Deadpool, Ubisoft, Disneyland, Netflix, Gmail, Seahawks, Celtics. The activation sits on the name token itself, or on the last subword of a split name. It is weaker on some concrete common nouns used as topic heads (kittens, bullets, drills, ammo, hiatus, Scrabble, 'important'). An emoji that directly follows another emoji (🤣 after 😀) can also go positive.

L28_N9555_neg.wrong_label: Content words naming the topic of research in academic, educational or cognitive-science prose, especially what people learn, do, understand or decide. Examples: 'student' in 'Using student assessment', 'professional', 'metaphors', 'decision(-making)', 'understand', 'negotiate', 'repair', 'trigonometry', 'Geoscience Students', 'classrooms', 'artefacts', 'product development', 'problem solving at', 'reasoning', 'writing', 'spelling', 'breathing'. Also fires on the first word of a topic span ('up to', 'at multiple').

L28_N9555_pos.wrong_label: The dominant pole: concepts of being at the periphery, outside, leftover or marginal. The activation lands on the content word that carries that meaning, usually its first or head subword. Examples: 'Outs'(iders) -10; '(homeless out)casts' -7; 'last bit (of carbon) that' -8/-6; 'fillet production' (a by-product source) -7; 'frowned on' -6; 'product left at the end' -6/-4; 'things you would…' (cast-offs/donations) -6; 'falls outside of the mainstream' -5; 'those most oppressed' -5/-4; 'downsizing' -5; 'oddball' -5; 'in the shadows' -5; 'cracks of our community' -4; 'end of the season' -3; 'beyond the edge' -3; 'spare' -3; 'languished in the background' -3. Nearby tokens such as 'of', 'the' and 'in' within the phrase get -1 to -2.

L32_N0133_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that refer to a small set of people or animate entities treated as one collective unit, especially pairs and trios acting or described together. Typical triggers are 'Two Friends', 'tandem of', 'trio', 'twins', 'brothers', 'sisters', 'young men from different', 'both … and', 'they' (when referring back to a pair or group), 'on either side', 'two vehicles' (in a collision between two). Activation lands on the group noun or quantifier ('friends', 'trio', 'twins', 'tandem', 'of' after 'tandem' or 'group') or on the anaphoric 'they'/'both'. It is strongest in narrative or descriptive prose about people jointly doing or being something.

L32_N1303_neg.wrong_label: Matter-of-fact, journalistic (often news or sports) references to a collective entity's own possession, belonging or condition ('in their own conditions', 'on their home turf', 'it was all Big Horn', 'continue to belong to the same circuit', 'Japan is a signatory', 'the Jewish community', 'Georgia's democracy is', 'the nation's plunge', 'boost the share of', 'print our logo'). L32_N1398_neg.wrong_label: Tokens that open or set up a duration or interval, where the model expects a span to follow: 'between', 'from' (as in from X to Y), 'over the last/past', 'during the period of', 'throughout', 'in the past', 'ranging', 'spans', 'since then'. Activation peaks on the word right before the span's content begins. That is usually the space/number-start token after 'of'/'from', or 'between', 'that' in 'over that same period', or 'last'/'past'. - Sentence-final '.' after legal, terms-of-service or methods sentences ('...changes to our website.', '...measurements.', '...pain is reproduced.', '...characterized.').

Date ranges inside career lines are moderately negative ('from 2001-02', '2002-2004').

L32_N3213_neg.wrong_label: Comparative-degree and magnitude-intensifier words that set up a comparison: 'more' (especially 'more than' and 'more likely to'), 'greater impact on', 'even further', 'twice' / 'three times', comparative adjectives ('bigger', 'younger', 'stronger', 'smoother', 'better', 'different'). L32_N3213_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token right BEFORE a token the model expects to begin with 'pe'/'Pe'/'PE' or 'pe'-like subword pieces. Typical continuations: pepper ('salt and|' → pepper, 'black|' → pepper), peek ('sneak|' → peek), peptide ('forms of|' → peptides, 'ply|' → peptide), peas ('can of|'), peat, PEIS ('Solar|'), pecker ('Wood|'), -peak ('Easy-S|'), and brand or person names already seen in the passage: PeepSo, Peppers, Peeters, Peet, Pepperdine, Peugeot, APEX. Magnitude is strongest when earlier context has already primed a specific Pe-word, e.g. a name repeated through the passage.

L32_N4182_neg.wrong_label: Tokens inside cheerful, promotional or warmly evaluative phrases that build toward a pleasant payoff for the reader or speaker. Typical frames: "cross one more thing off", "fill the house with the warm smell", "miss out on some fun", "nice to have something to look forward to", "so show off your spirit", "what better way to spend it", "can now show off", "have something novel to promote", "more information than ever", "more affordable than ever", "made easy", "how exciting my life is". The peak usually lands on the function or quantifier word just before the payoff, not on the payoff noun itself: "more" in "one more thing", "with" in "fill…with", "some" in "some fun", "something/to" in "something to look forward to", "to" in "way to spend", "from" in "away from", "now" in "can now", "of" in "at the bottom of". Weaker positive firing appears in some light number contexts, e.g. "that's equal to", "(24 y", "the 7,000".

L32_N4362_neg.wrong_label: The positive pole is weak, at most about +2. It fires on second or later word pieces of words starting with combining prefixes such as multi-, cross-, double-, short-, half-. Examples: 'isc' in multid|isc|iplinary, '-check' in cross-check, 'er' in crosser, 'plies' in multiplies, '-colored' in multi-colored. It also catches 'ictions' in addictions, 'ject' in between-subject, and 'udes' in alludes. Phrase-final function words after quantity words give about +1: 'full of', 'half of', 'long enough', 'multiple times', 'combined with'.

L32_N4362_pos.wrong_label: Tokens that introduce or complete the stopping condition of an ongoing activity, i.e. the point at which something ends. The strongest trigger is the connector itself: 'until' ('bake 15–18 minutes or until tops are firm', 'contest will continue until', 'repeating until Saturday', 'runs until 20.'), the 'as' of 'as long as' / 'as long as needed', and 'if' in 'taste to see if'. Words naming cessation also fire: 'Termination', 'stopping', 'stop', 'leave the tent', 'how long is desirable to keep'. The punctuation or end word that closes a completion condition fires too: the comma after 'check the fire was fully out,', '...the itch is still there to play,', 'clean' in 'toothpick comes out clean', the period after 'jiggly in the middle.'. In recipes, 'or' in 'X minutes or until' and the doneness word ('desired', 'set') get moderate activation.

L32_N4386_neg.wrong_label: Fires on copular or stative 'be' and 'become', especially right after infinitival 'to' or a verb like want/need/decided/able. Examples: 'decided to «become»' −10, 'wanted to «be»' −9, 'cannot «be»' −8, 'needed to «be»' −7, 'to «be» inspired/cautious/listed/able' −6 to −7. The element right after that 'be' (a / on / adjective) is also negative, around −2 to −5. Related weaker negatives (−3 to −7) appear on non-object verbs or possessives where a state or self-reference is predicted rather than an acted-on object. Examples: 'look «your» best' −6, 'in front of «you»' −7, 'remain' −5, 'come' −3, and possessives 'your/our/my' after verbs at −1 to −4.

L32_N4954_neg.wrong_label:
Tokens inside stock, highly predictable phrases, where the continuation is nearly fixed. Typical sources are web boilerplate and set formulas:
- "By using our websites,"
- "Your continued use of"
- "By clicking AGREE … you confirm"
- "receive notifications of new posts by email"
- "Get every new post delivered to your Inbox"
- "Click Here To Check Price"
- "custom writing services"
- "Forward-looking statements are"
- "on your behalf"
- "appeared to be impaired" (police-report style)
- "take away the sins of many" (scripture)
- year ranges like "from 2007 to 2012" (the year digit after "20" and the word "to" fire)

The peak lands on the word that commits to or continues the template, such as "use", "confirm", "receive", "delivered", "services", "to", the year digit, or a comma after a fixed opener. L32_N4954_pos.wrong_label: Fires on the token that completes a word or acronym built from a 'B' followed by an h/l/ul sound, i.e. the continuation right after a B-initial piece. Examples: 'hole(s)' after 'black' (+7 to +10; 'Blackhole' +8); 'H' after B in acronyms like DBH, KBH, BH&H (+8/+9), with a following '&H' at +5; 'bully/bullying' and the 'lying' in 'Bul|lying' (+5 to +7); 'ies'/'y' after 'Balcon' (+6/+8); 'hd' in 'Bag|hd|ad' (+4/+5); 'Bh/BH/bh' starts as in Bhakti or a mushroom bh(aji) (+3 to +5); 'HE' in 'B|HE|C' (+5); 'ulg' in 'B|ulg|arian' (+4); Kabul (+3); Ozub|ulu (+3); Wil|bur (+2); balcony/Balkans (+1 to +2). L32_N5221_neg.wrong_label: Fires on an early sub-word piece of an unusual proper name or foreign word, where the model must commit to completing a specific memorized name. Typical tokens: the first capital piece or a hyphen-joined piece. Examples: 'V' in La Venta and Rincón de la Viejá, '-D' in Scooby-Doo, 'Am' in Amrou and Amalia, 'Tro' in Trooper, '-X' in Jávea-Xàbia, 'sol' in solohsu, 'Rob' in Robidas, 'P' in Pannu, 'De' in Dean & DeLuca, 'M' in Mute Swan, 'Reb' in Rebney, 'Rev' in Revit. Examples: 'and' / 'Consumer' / 'Street' in the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act; 'Support' in My Oracle Support; 'Public' in View Public Profile; 'is' in 'This is an older thread'; 'or' in 'Pagination or Media Count'; 'resolve' / 'over' in 'a 6ya expert can help you resolve that issue over the phone'; 'Member' in Silver Member.

L32_N5714_neg.wrong_label:

- The 7 itself (-2 to -8), e.g. '5-7 business days' 7 = -10, '(7 Working Days)' 7 = -5 to -8.

A second cluster is color or garment words in product descriptions: 'navy' -8/-9, 'dark' -4, '/black' -7, 'Neck'(lace) -9, 'lace' -6. Also some isolated sports or name tokens: 'rebounds' -8, 'LRR' -8, 'Lennon' -3, 'Strip' -2, 'Red' -1 to -3.

L32_N6086_neg.wrong_label: First subword fragment of an unusual or foreign capitalized word or name, typically right after a newline or opening parenthesis, where the word is split into pieces: 'Ter|mination', 'Em|erson', 'Em|ery', 'Ar|abic', 'Be|ckum', 'Se|oul', 'Ro|aming', 'Ly|ra', 'Sylv|ie', 'Wo|erk', '.W' in 'C.W.', 'Tenn.', 'Bar|uch'. Only the first fragment fires. Activation is strongest (+3 to +4) when the line starts with a subword like 'Em', 'Ter', 'Ep', 'Ro', 'Se'.

L32_N6505_neg.wrong_label: The main pole. Fires on the final subword token that completes a plural noun, especially when the plural ending is fused into a word-piece after a split, as in 'micro|scopes', 'Ele|phants', 'Orch|ids', 'ga|uges', 'Purch|asers', 'Be|asts', 'Cou|gars', 'Cut|ters', 'free|zers', 'Buff|s'. Whole-word plural tokens such as 'consoles', 'chains', 'players', 'slaves', 'volunteers' and 'gems' also fire, usually more weakly (-1 to -3). The strongest cases (-7 to -10) are concrete, countable things or animals, product categories, and team names.

L32_N6505_pos.wrong_label: Language about time, attention, space or energy as a limited resource being consumed or fought over. Examples: 'never enough time' (time -5), 'number of hours people work' (hours -5), '12 hours a day' (-3/-4), 'focus on' (-4), 'work-life balance' (-4), 'devote time to' (-4/-3), 'finding time' (-4), 'precious pack space/energy' (-3/-4), 'clog things up' (-4), 'staff reduced' (-4), 'take up the bulk of my attention' (-2/-4).
